definition_zh: 破产的；资不抵债的；（品质上）彻底缺乏的；破产者；使破产
definition_en: unable to pay what one owes, or legally declared unable to do so; also completely lacking a quality, and to make a person or firm legally unable to pay debts
core_image: 一张被劈成两半的换钱长凳，账本还摊在断口上，主人站在一旁
scene: 几轮投机失败之后，那家老牌商号在春天被法院宣告破产。After several failed speculations, the old trading house was declared bankrupt that spring.
sceneCN: 几轮投机失败之后，那家老牌商号在春天被法院宣告破产；句中的 bankrupt 指「依法被认定无力清偿债务」（第 1 个义项：经法律程序宣告无力偿债）。图中可辨识物件：劈开的木柜台、散落的账本、法院封条、空钱袋。

pos.zh: 破产的；资不抵债的；（品质）彻底缺乏的
破产者；破产企业
使破产；使彻底失败

senses.title: Declared unable to pay by a court
senses.titleCN: 经法院程序宣告无力偿债
senses.definition: legally declared unable to pay one's debts, and therefore subject to bankruptcy proceedings
senses.definitionCN: 被法律宣告无力清偿债务，因而进入破产程序
senses.example: After several failed speculations, the old trading house was declared bankrupt that spring.
senses.exampleCN: 几轮投机失败之后，那家老牌商号在春天被法院宣告破产。
senses.why: The Italian image behind the word is a money changer's bench broken in two, and the courtroom later took that market picture as a formal legal status.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的意大利语意象是一张被劈开的换钱长凳，后来法庭把这个市场画面接过去，用作正式的法律状态。

senses.title: Owing more than one can ever pay
senses.titleCN: 资不抵债、实际无力偿还
senses.definition: in fact unable to meet one's debts, whether or not a court has ruled on it
senses.definitionCN: 事实上无力偿还债务，无论法院是否已作出裁定
senses.example: The mill had been bankrupt in all but name for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家磨坊两年来名不副实，实际上早已资不抵债。
senses.why: The broken bench came before any judge did: a trader whose credit had collapsed was finished in the market long before the paperwork arrived.
senses.whyCN: 断凳出现在法官之前：信用崩塌的商人在市场上早已完结，文书只是后来才到。

senses.title: A person or firm in that condition
senses.definition: a person or business that has been legally declared unable to pay its debts
senses.definitionCN: 已被法律宣告无力偿债的个人或企业
senses.example: The trustee sold the bankrupt's remaining stock at auction.
senses.exampleCN: 受托人把破产者剩下的存货拍卖掉了。
senses.why: English first used the word for the person standing at the broken bench, and the noun sense has stayed beside the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 英语最初用这个词指站在断凳边的那个人，名词义一直与形容词义并存。

senses.title: To ruin someone financially
senses.definition: to cause a person or company to lose all their money and become unable to pay debts
senses.definitionCN: 使个人或公司失去全部资金、无力偿债
senses.example: The flood bankrupted three family farms in one season.
senses.exampleCN: 那场洪水在一个季节里让三个家庭农场破产。
senses.why: The verb is the adjective turned into an action: putting someone at the broken bench.
senses.whyCN: 动词义就是把形容词变成动作：把某人推到那张断凳前。

senses.title: Completely lacking a quality
senses.definition: completely without a good quality such as honesty or moral seriousness
senses.definitionCN: 完全不具备诚实、道义感之类的好品质
senses.example: The report called the scheme morally bankrupt.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称这项计划在道德上已经破产。
senses.why: A bench stripped of its goods is empty; a person stripped of a quality is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 柜台被搬空就是空的；一个人被剥去某种品质，也用同一个词来形容。

senses.title: Collapsed as a plan or policy
senses.definition: having failed completely and lost all support or credibility
senses.definitionCN: 彻底失败，失去一切支持或可信度
senses.example: By the third year the housing policy was politically bankrupt.
senses.exampleCN: 到第三年，这项住房政策在政治上已经彻底失去支持。
senses.why: A plan whose backing disappears fails the way a firm fails when its credit disappears, so the financial word was extended to ideas.
senses.whyCN: 支持消失的计划，垮掉的方式正如信用消失的企业，于是这个财务词被延伸到观念上。

senses.title: Drained of resources or ideas
senses.definition: having used up the supply of something needed, such as energy, nutrients or new ideas
senses.definitionCN: 把所需的某种供给用尽，如能量、养分或新想法
senses.example: Years of single cropping left the soil bankrupt of nutrients.
senses.exampleCN: 多年单一种植使土壤的养分被耗尽。
senses.why: Treating a supply as capital makes running out of it a kind of bankruptcy.
senses.whyCN: 把某种储备当作资本看待，用光它也就成了一种破产。

senses.title: Belonging to bankruptcy proceedings
senses.titleCN: 属于破产程序的（作定语）
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark property, sales or records that belong to a bankruptcy case
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标记属于破产案件的财产、出售或记录
senses.example: Buyers flocked to the bankrupt estate sale on the pier.
senses.exampleCN: 买家涌向码头那场破产财产拍卖。
senses.why: Once bankruptcy became a legal procedure, the old adjective turned into a classifier for everything the procedure touches.
senses.whyCN: 破产成为法律程序之后，这个旧形容词就变成分类词，标记该程序所触及的一切。

intro.en: Bankrupt is generally traced to Italian banca rotta, literally 'broken bench', the failure of a money changer whose table was smashed. It reached English through French forms in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bankrupt 一般认为来自意大利语 banca rotta，字面意思是「断掉的凳子」，指换钱商的柜台被砸、生意垮台。它在十六世纪经法语形式进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Banca meant a bench or table, the counter where a money changer worked; rotta meant broken, from Latin rupta.
items.cn: banca 指长凳或桌子，即换钱商工作的柜台；rotta 意为折断的，出自拉丁语 rupta。

items.en: Rumpere 'to break' supplied ruptus 'broken' and is the source of rupture, corrupt and disrupt; the image is a solid thing split apart.
items.cn: 拉丁语 rumpere「折断」给出 ruptus「折断的」，也是 rupture、corrupt 与 disrupt 的来源；意象是一件坚实之物被劈开。

items.en: In Italian market squares a changer who could not settle his debts might have his bench broken, a public sign that he could no longer trade.
items.cn: 在意大利的集市广场上，无法清偿债务的换钱商可能被砸掉柜台，这是公开宣告他不能再做生意。

items.en: French forms such as banqueroute carried the word into English, where it first named the ruined trader rather than the legal state.
items.cn: banqueroute 之类的法语形式把这个词带进英语，最初指垮掉的商人，而不是法律状态。

items.en: Nineteenth-century insolvency statutes fixed bankrupt as a formal status distinct from merely owing money, and the procedural sense followed.
items.cn: 十九世纪的无力偿债法把 bankrupt 固定为一种正式身份，与单纯欠钱区分开来，程序义随后产生。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the broken-bench root or look alike; group two holds words for being unable to pay.
note.cn: 第一组是共享「折断」词根或形近的词；第二组是表示无力偿债的词。

entries.definition: From the same Italian bench word, but it names the institution that sits behind the counter, not the failure of one.
entries.definitionCN: 同出意大利语的「长凳」一词，但指柜台背后的机构，不指其垮台。

entries.definition: Built on the same Latin verb for breaking; it means a split or tear, often of a pipe or a relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 同出表示「折断」的拉丁动词，指裂口或断裂，常指管道或关系。

entries.definition: Literally 'broken through and through', from the same root; it means morally spoiled, not financially ruined.
entries.definitionCN: 字面是「彻底被破坏」，同出这个词根；意指道德败坏，不是财务破产。

entries.definition: To break apart the normal course of something, from the same breaking verb, with no financial meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事的正常进程打断，同出「折断」动词，与财务无关。

entries.definition: The accounting term for owing more than one's assets are worth; it states the balance sheet, not the broken bench.
entries.definitionCN: 会计术语，指负债超过资产价值；它陈述资产负债表，不带断凳意象。

entries.definition: Everyday word for having no money at all, usually said of a person and often temporary.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指身上一点钱也没有，多用于个人，常是暂时的。

entries.definition: Destroyed financially or otherwise; it can cover reputation and property as well as money.
entries.definitionCN: 在财务或其他方面被毁掉；除金钱外还可指名声与财产。

entries.definition: Used of a business that has stopped operating; it reports the outcome without the legal weight of bankrupt.
entries.definitionCN: 用于已停止运营的企业；只报告结果，没有 bankrupt 的法律分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Italian bench plus broken: the counter itself is snapped, so no trade can continue.
normal.cn: 意大利语的「长凳」加「折断」：柜台本身被劈开，生意自然做不下去。

normal.en: The family runs bankrupt, bankruptcy and bankruptcies.
normal.cn: 同族词有 bankrupt、bankruptcy 与 bankruptcies。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: go bankrupt, declare somebody bankrupt, morally bankrupt.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：破产倒闭、宣告某人破产、道德败坏。

normal.en: The same Latin breaking verb appears in rupture, corrupt and disrupt.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁「折断」动词出现在 rupture、corrupt 与 disrupt 中。

normal.en: Legal usage keeps the adjective before nouns: bankrupt estate, bankrupt sale.
normal.cn: 法律用法让这个形容词留在名词前：破产财产、破产拍卖。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden counter split down the middle while the ledgers stay open on both halves.
abstract.cn: 想象一张木柜台从中间裂开，账本还摊在两半上。

abstract.en: Picture a wallet with a hole in the lining, so every coin leaves as soon as it enters.
abstract.cn: 想象一只内衬破洞的钱包，硬币一进去就漏出来。

abstract.en: Picture a chair whose legs are gone, still labelled as a chair by a small brass plate.
abstract.cn: 想象一把腿都没了的椅子，还挂着一块小铜牌称它为椅子。

examples.en: The airline went bankrupt after two years of losses.
examples.cn: 这家航空公司在连续两年亏损后破产了。

examples.en: A single bad harvest can bankrupt a smallholder who has borrowed for seed.
examples.cn: 一次歉收就能让借钱买种子的佃农破产。

examples.en: Critics called the reform morally bankrupt because it punished the poorest.
examples.cn: 批评者称这项改革在道德上已经破产，因为它惩罚了最穷的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 柜台被劈断，账本散落：商号再也做不成买卖 → 破产

root: 意大利语 banca rotta「断掉的柜台」= banca「长凳、柜台」+ rotta「折断的」，rotta 出自拉丁语 rumpere「折断」；英语经法语形式进入，最初指破产的商人。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one broken counter: the legal ruling, the plain fact of insolvency, the person, the act of ruining, the loss of a quality, the collapse of a plan, the draining of a supply, and finally the courtroom label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕一张被劈开的柜台：法院裁定、实际资不抵债、破产的人、使人破产的动作、品质的丧失、计划的崩溃、储备的耗尽，最后是法庭上的分类标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a money changer's bench snapped in two, ledgers still lying on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被劈成两半的换钱长凳，账本还摊在上面。

branches.en: BROKEN BENCH: the courtroom ruling and the plain fact of owing more than one owns are the same image seen with and without a judge.
branches.cn: 断凳：法院裁定与实际资不抵债，是同一画面在有法官与无法官时的两种看法。

branches.en: PERSON AND ACT: the one who stands at the broken bench, and the act of putting someone there.
branches.cn: 人与动作：站在断凳前的那个人，以及把某人推到那里的动作。

branches.en: EMPTY COUNTER: a bench stripped of its goods becomes a person stripped of a quality.
branches.cn: 空柜台：被搬空货物的柜台，变成被剥去某种品质的人。

branches.en: FAILED SUPPORT: a policy and a supply of ideas give way the way credit gives way.
branches.cn: 支持崩塌：政策与点子储备的垮掉，正如信用的垮掉。

branches.en: COURTROOM LABEL: procedure turns the old adjective into a classifier for property and records.
branches.cn: 法庭标签：程序把这个旧形容词变成财产与记录的分类词。

intro.en: Bankrupt is an Italian phrase frozen into one word, and its breaking root also builds several English words.
intro.cn: bankrupt 是一个凝固成单词的意大利语短语，其中「折断」的词根还构成若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin rumpere gives rupture, corrupt and disrupt; the Italian bench word gives bank and bankrupt.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rumpere 衍生 rupture、corrupt 与 disrupt；意大利语的「长凳」一词给出 bank 与 bankrupt。

items.example: The bench stood at the corner of the market square.
items.exampleCN: 那张长凳摆在集市广场的角上。

items.example: The broken table could no longer hold a scale.
items.exampleCN: 那张折断的桌子再也放不住秤。

items.example: The root pictures a solid object split apart.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘一件坚实之物被劈开。

items.example: The trading house was declared bankrupt.
items.exampleCN: 那家商号被宣告破产。

items.meaning: the state or procedure of being bankrupt
items.example: The filing brought years of debt to a close.
items.exampleCN: 这次申请让多年的债务告一段落。

items.example: A rupture in the pipe flooded the cellar.
items.exampleCN: 管道破裂，淹了地窖。

items.meaning: broken through and through; morally spoiled
items.example: The inspectors were accused of taking bribes.
items.exampleCN: 检查人员被控收受贿赂。

items.meaning: to break apart the normal course
items.example: Fog disrupted flights for two days.
items.exampleCN: 大雾使航班中断了两天。

definition_zh: 纳税人；纳税的个人或企业；（作定语）由纳税人负担的
definition_en: a person or organization that is required by law to pay taxes to a government
core_image: 四月里邮局柜台前的一叠报税表，每张表后面都站着一个要交钱的人
scene: 每年四月，街角邮局里排队寄表的人格外多。Every April the queue at the corner post office is full of taxpayers mailing their returns.
sceneCN: 每年四月，街角邮局里排队寄表的人格外多；句中的 taxpayers 指「按法律申报并缴纳个人所得税的人」（第 1 个义项：个人所得税纳税人）。图中可辨识物件：报税表、信封、邮局柜台、排队的背影。

pos.zh: 纳税人；纳税的个人或企业
由纳税人负担的；纳税人的

forms.label: 合成定语（由纳税人出资的）

senses.title: A person who files and pays income tax
senses.titleCN: 申报并缴纳个人所得税的人
senses.definition: an individual who is legally required to report income and pay tax on it
senses.definitionCN: 依法须申报收入并就其缴纳个税的个人
senses.example: Every April the queue at the corner post office is full of taxpayers mailing their returns.
senses.exampleCN: 每年四月，街角邮局里排队寄表的人格外多，都是寄报税表的纳税人。
senses.why: Tax names the charge and payer names the one who settles it, so a single word marks the person on the paying side of the fiscal relation.
senses.whyCN: tax 指这笔课征，payer 指付清它的人，合起来就标记出财政关系里付钱的一方。

senses.title: A company or body that pays tax
senses.definition: a business or institution legally liable for tax on its profits, property or activities
senses.definitionCN: 就利润、财产或经营活动依法负税的企业或机构
senses.example: The levy falls on corporate taxpayers with plants in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这项课征落在本地区设有工厂的企业纳税人身上。
senses.why: Fiscal law treats a company as a person for tax purposes, so the same word covers a firm as well as an individual.
senses.whyCN: 税法在税务上把公司当作一个「人」，因此同一个词既指个人也指企业。

senses.title: The taxed public, seen against government
senses.titleCN: 与政府相对的纳税公众
senses.definition: the body of citizens considered as the source of public money, especially in political argument
senses.definitionCN: 在政治争论中被视为公共资金来源的公民整体
senses.example: The mayor asked taxpayers to judge the plan at the next hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 市长请纳税人在下一次听证会上评判这项计划。
senses.why: Once tax funding became the normal source of public services, the word turned into a political name for the paying side.
senses.whyCN: 当税收成为公共服务的常规财源，这个词就变成政治语境里「付钱一方」的称呼。

senses.title: Whoever ends up bearing a public cost
senses.titleCN: 最终替某项公共开支买单的人（比喻）
senses.definition: used figuratively for the people who ultimately bear the cost of a public project or mistake
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指最终承担某项公共工程或失误代价的人
senses.example: When the stadium overran its budget, local taxpayers picked up the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 体育场预算超支后，账单落到了当地纳税人头上。
senses.why: The literal payer of tax stands for anyone left holding the cost when public money runs short.
senses.whyCN: 字面上交税的人，被用来代替公共资金不足时被迫承担代价的任何人。

senses.title: A resident registered for local tax
senses.titleCN: 在辖区登记纳税的居民纳税人
senses.definition: a resident who is registered with a local authority and pays local taxes there
senses.definitionCN: 在地方当局登记并在当地纳税的居民
senses.example: Only residents registered as taxpayers in the district may vote on the school levy.
senses.exampleCN: 只有在本区登记为纳税人的居民才能就学校课征投票。
senses.why: Local revenue systems attach the word to a register, so taxpayer becomes a legal category tied to a place.
senses.whyCN: 地方财政制度把这个词挂在登记册上，纳税人因此成为与地点绑定的法律类别。

senses.title: Someone liable for one particular tax
senses.titleCN: 某一具体税种的纳税义务人
senses.definition: a person who is the legal subject of a specific duty, such as a property or land tax
senses.definitionCN: 某项具体税负的法律主体，如房产税或土地税的义务人
senses.example: Owners of the riverside plots become taxpayers under the new land levy.
senses.exampleCN: 根据新的土地课征，河岸地块的所有人成为纳税人。
senses.why: Each tax statute defines its own payer, so the word can be narrowed to whoever that statute names.
senses.whyCN: 每一部税法都自行界定付税人，因此这个词可以收窄到该法所指的那个人。

senses.title: The tax base as a group
senses.titleCN: 作为整体的纳税人群体与税基
senses.definition: the whole group of people and firms whose payments fund public spending, viewed as a pool
senses.definitionCN: 其缴款支撑公共支出的全部个人与企业，被看作一个池子
senses.example: A shrinking workforce means a smaller pool of taxpayers for the pension fund.
senses.exampleCN: 劳动人口萎缩意味着养老基金的纳税人池子变小。
senses.why: Counting payers together turns the word into a quantity that planners can measure and project.
senses.whyCN: 把付税人合起来数，这个词就变成一个规划者可以衡量与预测的数量。

senses.title: Used before a noun: paid for by taxpayers
senses.titleCN: 作定语：由纳税人出资的
senses.definition: placed before a noun to say that the thing named is financed by public tax money
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示所指数事物由公共税款出资
senses.example: The bridge was rebuilt with taxpayer money, not private capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是用纳税人的钱重建的，不是私人资本。
senses.why: The attributive use compresses a whole sentence about funding into a label attached to the object.
senses.whyCN: 定语用法把一整句关于出资的话压缩成贴在物件上的标签。

intro.en: Taxpayer joins two Latin-derived words: tax, from taxare 'to assess or charge', and payer, from pacare 'to settle or pacify'. The compound is an English formation of the modern fiscal state. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: taxpayer 由两个源自拉丁语的词合成：tax 出自 taxare「评估、课征」，payer 出自 pacare「平息、清偿」。这个复合词是近代财政国家形成后的英语构词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Taxare meant 'to assess, evaluate, charge', originally a frequentative of tangere 'to touch', as if a value were felt out by hand.
items.cn: taxare 意为「评估、估量、课征」，原是 tangere「触摸」的反复动词，仿佛用手摸出价值。

items.en: Medieval Latin taxa named an assessed charge, and the noun passed into English as a levy imposed by authority.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 taxa 指经评估确定的课征额，这个名词进入英语后指当局征收的税。

items.en: Pacare 'to pacify' developed the sense 'to settle a debt, satisfy a creditor', which became the everyday verb to pay.
items.cn: pacare「使平息」引申出「清偿债务、使债主满意」的意思，后来成为日常动词「付钱」。

items.en: English built taxpayer from tax plus payer, naming the person on the paying side once taxation became routine and bureaucratized.
items.cn: 英语用 tax 加 payer 造出 taxpayer，在征税变得常规化、官僚化之后，用来指付钱的一方。

items.en: The spread of income tax in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries made the word a standard political term, and the attributive use followed.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪所得税的普及使这个词成为标准政治用语，定语用法也随之出现。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same tax stem but naming different things; group two holds words for people who pay or are counted by a revenue system.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「税」词干但所指不同的词；第二组是收入体系中付钱或被计入的人。

entries.definition: The compulsory payment or the statute that imposes it; taxpayer names the person, not the payment.
entries.definitionCN: 指强制缴纳的款项或课征法规；taxpayer 指人，不指款项。

entries.definition: An adjective for income or goods that fall within the scope of a tax, whether or not anyone actually pays.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指收入或货物在征税范围内，不论实际是否有人缴款。

entries.definition: The whole activity or system of raising revenue by taxes, not any single payer within it.
entries.definitionCN: 指整套征税活动或制度，不是其中某个付税人。

entries.definition: The adjective describing the public as people who pay tax, as in the taxpaying public.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述缴税的公众，如「纳税公众」。

entries.definition: A British term for someone who pays local property-based rates; narrower than taxpayer, which covers all taxes.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指缴纳地方房产税的人；比涵盖各类税的 taxpayer 窄。

entries.definition: A person who submits a tax return; the emphasis is on the form, not on the money paid.
entries.definitionCN: 指提交报税表的人；重点在表格，不在缴款。

entries.definition: A member of a state with rights and duties; taxpayer picks out only the fiscal duty.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有权利与义务的国家成员；taxpayer 只挑出财政义务。

entries.definition: Someone who lives in a place; many residents are taxpayers, but the words mark different facts.
entries.definitionCN: 在某地居住的人；许多居民是纳税人，但两个词标记的是不同事实。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Tax plus payer: the charge on one side, the one who settles it on the other.
normal.cn: 「税」加「付钱者」：一边是课征，一边是清偿它的人。

normal.en: The family runs taxpayer, taxpayers, taxpaying and taxpayer-funded.
normal.cn: 同族词有 taxpayer、taxpayers、taxpaying 与 taxpayer-funded。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: individual taxpayer, corporate taxpayer, taxpayer money.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：个人纳税人、企业纳税人、纳税人的钱。

normal.en: Payer comes from the Latin verb for settling a debt, not from the noun for money.
normal.cn: payer 出自拉丁语中「清偿债务」的动词，并非出自表示钱的名词。

normal.en: Budget debates pair it with spending: taxpayer money funds public services.
normal.cn: 预算辩论把它与支出配对：公共服务的资金来自纳税人的钱。

abstract.en: Picture a long queue where each person hands over a folded form and keeps the carbon copy.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长队，每人交出一张折好的表格，自己留下复写的那一联。

abstract.en: Picture a reservoir fed by thousands of small pipes, each labelled with a household name.
abstract.cn: 想象一座水库由成千根细管供水，每根管子上都写着一个家庭的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt handed back to the person who paid, while the goods go to everyone.
abstract.cn: 想象收据交回给付钱的人，而货物送给所有人。

examples.en: The agency publishes a guide for first-time taxpayers each winter.
examples.cn: 该机构每年冬天为首次纳税的人发布指南。

examples.en: Corporate taxpayers may offset part of the loss against next year's profit.
examples.cn: 企业纳税人可用部分亏损抵扣来年利润。

examples.en: Voters complained that taxpayer money was spent on a private consultant.
examples.cn: 选民抱怨纳税人的钱花在了一名私人顾问身上。

root: 英语复合词：tax（出自拉丁 taxare「评估、课征」）+ payer（出自拉丁 pacare「平息、清偿」，即付钱者）；指依法缴税的个人或企业。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the paying side of a fiscal relation: the individual filer, the corporate payer, the public facing government, the figurative bearer of cost, the local registrant, the subject of one tax, the collective tax base, and the attributive label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿财政关系中付钱的一方展开：个人申报者、企业缴款者、与政府相对的公众、比喻中的买单者、地方登记纳税人、某一税种的义务人、作为整体的税基，最后是定语标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue of people handing folded forms across a counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人隔着柜台递上折好的表格。

branches.en: WHO PAYS: the individual at the counter and the company treated as a person for tax both fill the same role.
branches.cn: 谁在付：柜台前的个人与税务上被视为「人」的公司，扮演同一个角色。

branches.en: TWO SIDES: government collects, the paying public is named as the other side of that relation.
branches.cn: 两边：政府征收，纳税公众被命名为这段关系的另一边。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE BILL: whoever is left holding a public cost inherits the name of the literal payer.
branches.cn: 比喻账单：最终替公共开支兜底的人，继承了字面付税人的名号。

branches.en: LEGAL SUBJECT: a register in a district and a clause in a tax statute both single out the liable person.
branches.cn: 法律主体：辖区登记册与税法条文都挑出应负义务的那个人。

branches.en: COUNTED POOL: many payers become a base planners can measure, then a label for what the money buys.
branches.cn: 可数的池子：众多付税人成为规划者可衡量的税基，再变成所购之物的标签。

intro.en: Taxpayer is an English compound whose two halves each descend from a Latin verb, so the word reads as two actions joined.
intro.cn: taxpayer 是英语复合词，两半各自源自一个拉丁动词，因此这个词读起来是两个动作的结合。

latinIntro.en: Latin taxare supplies tax, taxable and taxation; Latin pacare supplies pay, payment and payer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 taxare 给出 tax、taxable 与 taxation；拉丁 pacare 给出 pay、payment 与 payer。

collocations.zh: 税收收入占经济总量的比重

senses.title: The government's total tax intake
senses.definition: the whole sum of money a government receives from all forms of taxation in a period
senses.definitionCN: 政府在一段时期内从各种税种取得的全部款项
senses.example: On the city hall ledger, the largest line comes from tax revenue raised on sales and income.
senses.exampleCN: 市政厅的年度账本上，最大的一栏来自销售税与所得税。
senses.why: Tax names the charge and revenue names what comes back in, so the phrase measures money flowing toward the treasury.
senses.whyCN: tax 指课征，revenue 指回流之物，因此这个短语衡量的是流向国库的钱。

senses.title: The yield of one particular tax
senses.definition: the amount produced by a single tax, such as a fuel duty or a property levy
senses.definitionCN: 由单一税种产生的金额，如燃料税或房产税
senses.example: Fuel duty remains the steadiest source of tax revenue in the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料税仍是预算中最稳定的税收收入来源。
senses.why: A total is made of parts, so the same phrase can name the contribution of any one tax.
senses.whyCN: 总额由各部分相加而成，因此同一短语也可指任一税种的贡献。

senses.title: Revenue collected by central government
senses.titleCN: 中央或联邦政府取得的税收收入
senses.definition: tax money that goes to the national treasury rather than to local authorities
senses.definitionCN: 进入国家国库而非地方财政的税款
senses.example: Central tax revenue covers defence, while councils rely on local levies.
senses.exampleCN: 中央税收收入支撑国防，地方议会则依赖本地课征。
senses.why: Revenue follows the level of government that imposes the tax, so the phrase splits along central and local lines.
senses.whyCN: 收入跟随课征它的政府层级，因此这个短语会按中央与地方分开。

senses.title: Revenue collected by local government
senses.titleCN: 地方政府取得的税收收入
senses.definition: tax money that stays with a city, county or regional authority
senses.definitionCN: 留在市、县或地区当局的税款
senses.example: Local tax revenue paid for the new tram line.
senses.exampleCN: 地方税收收入出资修建了新的有轨电车线路。
senses.why: The same treasury word is narrowed by the adjective local, marking which authority keeps the money.
senses.whyCN: 同一个国库用词被「地方」这个修饰语收窄，标明哪一级当局留下这笔钱。

senses.title: Net revenue after refunds
senses.titleCN: 扣除退税后的净税收收入
senses.definition: the amount left after refunds, credits and arrears are subtracted from gross collections
senses.definitionCN: 从征收总额中扣除退税、抵免与欠缴后剩下的金额
senses.example: Gross receipts looked healthy, but net tax revenue fell after refunds.
senses.exampleCN: 征收总额看着不错，但扣除退税后净税收收入下降了。
senses.why: Accounting separates what is collected from what is kept, so revenue can be reported gross or net.
senses.whyCN: 会计把「收上来」与「留下来」分开，因此收入可分毛额与净额报告。

senses.title: Tax take measured against the economy
senses.titleCN: 以经济总量为基准衡量的税负水平
senses.definition: tax receipts expressed as a proportion of national output, used to compare countries
senses.definitionCN: 以国民产出比例为尺度表示的税收，用于比较各国
senses.example: Tax revenue as a share of output rose three points in a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 税收收入占产出的比重在十年间上升了三个百分点。
senses.why: Comparing absolute sums across economies is misleading, so the phrase is turned into a ratio.
senses.whyCN: 直接比较不同经济体的绝对金额会误导，因此这个短语被转换成一个比率。

senses.title: The forecast figure in a budget
senses.titleCN: 预算中的税收收入估算
senses.definition: the projected amount of tax money that a budget expects to receive
senses.definitionCN: 预算预期将收到的税款估算额
senses.example: The forecast for tax revenue was cut by two billion.
senses.exampleCN: 预算中的税收收入估算被下调了二十亿。
senses.why: Governments must plan before money arrives, so revenue also names a number on a projection sheet.
senses.whyCN: 政府必须在钱到手前规划，因此收入也指预测表上的一个数字。

senses.title: Earmarked revenue for a specific purpose
senses.titleCN: 指定用途的专项税收收入
senses.definition: tax money legally reserved for one programme, such as roads or pensions
senses.definitionCN: 依法保留给某一项目使用的税款，如道路或养老金
senses.example: The fuel levy is earmarked tax revenue for road repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料课征是指定用于道路维修的专项税收收入。
senses.why: Once a tax is tied to a purpose, the revenue stops being general and becomes a dedicated stream.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某项税与某个用途绑定，这笔收入就不再是一般财源，而成为专款。

intro.en: Tax revenue joins tax, from Latin taxare 'to assess or charge', with revenue, from Latin revenire 'to come back' through Old French. The pair became standard in public finance. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tax revenue 由 tax 与 revenue 合成：tax 出自拉丁 taxare「评估、课征」，revenue 经古法语来自拉丁 revenire「回来」。这一搭配在公共财政中成为标准说法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Taxare 'to assess, charge' gave the noun tax, a levy fixed by authority after a valuation.
items.cn: taxare「评估、课征」给出名词 tax，即经估值后由当局确定的课征。

items.en: Revenire combined re- 'back' with venire 'to come', so the word pictured money coming back to the one who had laid it out.
items.cn: revenire 由「回」加 venire「来」构成，画面是钱回到当初支出它的人手里。

items.en: Old French revenue meant 'a return, an income', and English borrowed it for the income of an estate or a crown.
items.cn: 古法语 revenue 意为「回报、收入」，英语借来表示庄园或王室的收入。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century budgets paired the two words, making tax revenue the standard label for the state's tax income.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪的预算把这两个词配在一起，使 tax revenue 成为国家税收收入的标准标签。

items.en: Twentieth-century national accounts turned the phrase into a measured series, reported as a share of output and compared across countries.
items.cn: 二十世纪的国民核算把这个短语变成可测量的序列，按产出比重报告并用于国际比较。

note.en: Group one holds other tax compounds that look alike but measure different things; group two holds words for money coming in.
note.cn: 第一组是形近的其他「税」复合词，但衡量对象不同；第二组是表示进账的词。

entries.definition: The proportion at which income or goods are taxed; it scales the revenue rather than being the revenue.
entries.definitionCN: 指课税的比例，它决定收入的规模，本身不是收入。

entries.definition: The incomes, property or transactions that a tax reaches; revenue is the money actually raised from that base.
entries.definitionCN: 指税所触及的收入、财产或交易；收入是从这个税基实际征得的钱。

entries.definition: The weight of taxation on households or firms; it describes pressure, while revenue describes receipts.
entries.definitionCN: 指家庭或企业承受的税负压力；它描述压力，收入描述进账。

entries.definition: The document on which a taxpayer reports income; it is paperwork, not the money collected.
entries.definitionCN: 纳税人申报收入的文件；是文书，不是征得的钱。

entries.definition: Any money received, including fees, fines and sales; tax revenue is the slice that comes from taxes.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指一切收入，包括收费、罚金与销售；税收收入只是来自税的那一部分。

entries.definition: Money received by a person or business; it is not normally used for government receipts.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或企业收到的钱；一般不用来指政府进账。

entries.definition: The money actually received in a period, as recorded by an accountant; close to gross revenue.
entries.definitionCN: 会计记录中某期实际收到的钱，接近毛收入。

entries.definition: The money obtained from a particular sale, event or asset, not from taxation.
entries.definitionCN: 指某笔销售、活动或资产带来的钱，并非来自征税。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Tax plus revenue: what authority charges, and what comes back into the treasury.
normal.cn: 「税」加「回流之物」：当局课征什么，以及什么回到国库。

normal.en: The phrase has a plural for different taxes or years: tax revenues.
normal.cn: 不同税种或年度用复数：各类税收收入。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: total tax revenue, tax revenue growth, a shortfall in tax revenue.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：税收收入总额、税收收入增长、税收收入缺口。

normal.en: Revenue descends from a Latin verb meaning to come back, so the money is pictured returning.
normal.cn: revenue 出自意为「回来」的拉丁动词，因此这笔钱被设想成回流。

normal.en: Statistics compare it as a share of output, not as a raw sum.
normal.cn: 统计上以占产出的比重来比较它，而不是用绝对金额。

abstract.en: Picture a wide river fed by many narrow channels, each named after a different duty.
abstract.cn: 想象一条宽河由许多窄渠汇成，每条渠都以一种税命名。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where one bar is drawn longer than all the others combined.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，其中一根长条比其余所有加在一起还长。

abstract.en: Picture a tap that keeps dripping into a public jar while a queue fills cups from it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只龙头不断滴进公共的罐子，队伍从罐子里舀水。

examples.en: Rising wages pushed tax revenue above the official forecast.
examples.cn: 工资上涨使税收收入超过了官方预测。

examples.en: The province spends most of its tax revenue on schools and clinics.
examples.cn: 该省把大部分税收收入花在学校与诊所上。

examples.en: A tax revenue shortfall forced the council to delay repairs.
examples.cn: 税收收入缺口迫使议会推迟维修工程。

root: 英语复合短语：tax（出自拉丁 taxare「评估、课征」）+ revenue（经古法语来自拉丁 revenire「回来」，指进账）；指政府征税所得的总金额。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow money returning to the treasury: the national total, one tax's yield, central receipts, local receipts, net after refunds, the share of output, the budget forecast, and money tied to a purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿「钱回流国库」展开：全国总额、单一税种所得、中央收入、地方收入、退税后的净额、占产出的比重、预算估算，以及绑定用途的专款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide river of small payments converging into one treasury ledger.
core.cn: 核心意象：由无数小额缴款汇成的一条宽河，最终流进国库账本。

branches.en: COLLECTED MONEY: a total and one tax's share are the same flow at different scales.
branches.cn: 征收所得：总额与单一税种的份额，是同一条水流的不同尺度。

branches.en: LEVEL OF GOVERNMENT: central and local receipts split the same money by who keeps it.
branches.cn: 政府层级：中央与地方收入按「谁留下」把同一笔钱分开。

branches.en: NET FIGURE: refunds carve away part of the inflow before the balance is reported.
branches.cn: 净额：在报告余额之前，退税从流入中挖去一部分。

branches.en: RATIO VIEW: comparing economies turns the sum into a share of output.
branches.cn: 比率视角：比较不同经济体时，金额变成占产出的份额。

branches.en: PLANNED AND TIED: a forecast is money expected, and an earmark is money already promised.
branches.cn: 预算与专款：估算是预期中的钱，专项是已经许诺出去的钱。

intro.en: Tax revenue is an English compound of two Latin-derived words, one for charging and one for money returning.
intro.cn: tax revenue 是由两个源自拉丁语的词构成的英语复合短语，一个指课征，一个指钱回流。

latinIntro.en: Latin taxare supplies tax, taxable and taxation; Latin venire supplies revenue, convene and invent through related forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 taxare 给出 tax、taxable 与 taxation；拉丁 venire 经相关形式给出 revenue、convene 与 invent。

items.example: The assessor valued the land for tax.
items.exampleCN: 评估员为征税估定土地价值。

items.example: Rent is the estate's main revenue.
items.exampleCN: 租金是这份产业的主要收入。

items.example: Tax revenue rose with wages.
items.exampleCN: 税收收入随工资上涨而增加。

items.example: Only part of the gain is taxable.
items.exampleCN: 只有部分收益应纳税。

items.example: Taxation funds the courts.

items.example: The charity is tax-exempt.

definition_zh: 金融稳定；金融体系稳健；（监管语境）不出现系统性危机的状态
definition_en: the condition in which the financial system performs its functions without serious disruption or crisis
core_image: 一排立在地基上的柱子，每根都稳稳受力，没有一根开始倾斜
scene: 每年春天，央行都会发布一份报告，评估银行体系能否承受冲击。Every spring the central bank publishes a report on financial stability, asking whether banks can absorb shocks.
sceneCN: 每年春天，央行都会发布一份报告，评估银行体系能否承受冲击；句中的 financial stability 指「金融体系整体不出现系统性危机的状态」（第 1 个义项：金融体系整体稳定）。图中可辨识物件：报告封面、柱状图表、银行大楼、天平。

pos.zh: 金融稳定；金融体系稳健状态
金融稳定的；维护金融稳定的

senses.title: The system as a whole staying sound
senses.titleCN: 金融体系整体保持稳健
senses.definition: the state in which the whole financial system keeps working through shocks without a systemic crisis
senses.definitionCN: 整个金融体系在冲击下仍能运转、不爆发系统性危机的状态
senses.example: Every spring the central bank publishes a report on financial stability, asking whether banks can absorb shocks.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天，央行都会发布一份报告，评估银行体系能否承受冲击。
senses.why: Finance names the settling of debts and stability names standing firm, so the phrase pictures a debt system that does not topple.
senses.whyCN: finance 指债务的结清，stability 指站得稳，因此这个短语描绘的是一个不会倒下的债务体系。

senses.title: Banks and institutions being well capitalized
senses.titleCN: 金融机构资本充足、运转稳健
senses.definition: the soundness of individual banks and financial institutions, measured by capital, liquidity and asset quality
senses.definitionCN: 单个银行与金融机构的稳健程度，以资本、流动性与资产质量衡量
senses.example: Stress tests found the major banks sound enough to support financial stability.
senses.exampleCN: 压力测试发现各大银行足够稳健，可以支撑金融稳定。
senses.why: A system stands only if its members stand, so the phrase is also used of the institutions that make it up.
senses.whyCN: 体系只有成员站得住才站得住，因此这个短语也用于构成体系的机构。

senses.title: Prices and markets not swinging wildly
senses.titleCN: 市场价格与交易秩序平稳
senses.definition: the absence of extreme price swings, bubbles or market disruptions that damage confidence
senses.definitionCN: 不出现破坏信心的剧烈价格波动、泡沫或市场中断
senses.example: Regulators watched the housing market for signs that financial stability was at risk.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者密切注视房地产市场，寻找金融稳定受威胁的迹象。
senses.why: A market is stable when it can absorb shocks without violent swings, the same image of standing firm applied to prices.
senses.whyCN: 市场能吸收冲击而不剧烈摆动，就是稳定；同一「站得住」的画面被用到价格上。

senses.title: Households not overburdened with debt
senses.titleCN: 家庭财务稳健、债务可控
senses.definition: the condition of households whose debts and repayments remain manageable during downturns
senses.definitionCN: 家庭债务与还款在衰退期仍处于可控范围的状态
senses.example: High household debt is now treated as a risk to financial stability.
senses.exampleCN: 高企的家庭债务如今被视为对金融稳定的风险。
senses.why: When private balance sheets crack, the system cracks with them, so the phrase extends to the household level.
senses.whyCN: 私人资产负债表一旦裂开，体系也随之裂开，因此这个短语延伸到家庭层面。

senses.title: Firms able to service their debts
senses.titleCN: 企业财务稳健、偿债无碍
senses.definition: the condition of companies whose earnings cover their obligations even when conditions tighten
senses.definitionCN: 企业在环境收紧时收益仍能覆盖债务的状态
senses.example: Cheap credit had masked weak corporate financial stability.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价信贷掩盖了企业财务稳健性的薄弱。
senses.why: The corporate sector is another layer of the same standing structure, and its balance sheets carry the phrase's meaning.
senses.whyCN: 企业部门是同一稳固结构的又一层，其资产负债表承载着这个短语的含义。

senses.title: A mandate given to regulators
senses.titleCN: 监管当局承担的职责目标
senses.definition: the policy objective assigned to central banks and regulators, who must act before risks become crises
senses.definitionCN: 授予央行与监管机构的政策目标，须在风险演变为危机前行动
senses.example: The new law made financial stability an explicit mandate of the central bank.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律把金融稳定明确规定为央行的职责。
senses.why: A condition worth protecting becomes a duty once an institution is told to keep it, so the phrase turns into a mandate.
senses.whyCN: 一种值得守护的状态，在被指定给某个机构维持之后就变成职责，因此这个短语转为授权。

senses.title: Stability across borders
senses.titleCN: 国际与跨境的金融稳定
senses.definition: the shared condition of several national systems linked by trade, lending and capital flows
senses.definitionCN: 由贸易、借贷与资本流动联结的多个国家体系共同的稳定状态
senses.example: A currency run in one region can threaten financial stability elsewhere.
senses.exampleCN: 一个地区的挤兑可能威胁其他地区的金融稳定。
senses.why: Capital crosses borders faster than rules do, so the phrase is also used for the international layer of the same structure.
senses.whyCN: 资本跨境的速度快于规则，因此这个短语也用于同一结构的国际层面。

senses.title: A formal assessment of that condition
senses.titleCN: 金融稳定评估（报告与指标）
senses.definition: the periodic official assessment, with indicators and scenarios, of how far the system is from crisis
senses.definitionCN: 以指标与情景定期对体系距危机有多远所作的官方评估
senses.example: The autumn financial stability assessment flagged rising leverage.
senses.exampleCN: 秋季的金融稳定评估警示了杠杆上升。
senses.why: What is watched must be measured, so the name of the condition also labels the report that grades it.
senses.whyCN: 被守护的东西必须被测量，因此这种状态的名称也用来称呼为它打分的报告。

intro.en: Financial stability joins finance, from Old French finance 'settlement of a debt' and Latin finis 'end', with stability, from Latin stabilis 'firm' and stare 'to stand'. The pair became a policy term in the twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: financial stability 由 finance 与 stability 合成：finance 经古法语指「债务的结清」，源自拉丁 finis「终点」；stability 出自拉丁 stabilis「稳固」，再溯至 stare「站立」。这一搭配在二十世纪成为政策术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Finis meant 'end, boundary, limit'; settling a debt was pictured as bringing it to an end.
items.cn: finis 意为「终点、边界、限度」；结清债务被设想成把这件事带到终点。

items.en: Old French finance named the action of settling or paying, and English borrowed it for money matters and later for the management of money.
items.cn: 古法语 finance 指结清或支付的动作，英语借来表示钱财事务，后来又指资金管理。

items.en: Stare 'to stand' produced stabilis 'firm, standing steady', the root of stable, stability and stabilize.
items.cn: stare「站立」产生 stabilis「稳固、站得稳」，是 stable、stability 与 stabilize 的词根。

items.en: Twentieth-century central banking turned the two words into one term for the condition supervision exists to protect.
items.cn: 二十世纪的央行监管把这两个词合成一个术语，指监管所要守护的那种状态。

items.en: After the crises of the 1990s and 2008 the phrase became standard in international reports, with indicators, stress tests and periodic assessments.
items.cn: 经历九十年代与二零零八年的危机之后，这个短语成为国际报告的标准用语，配有指标、压力测试与定期评估。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring phrases built like this one but pointing at different objects; group two holds nouns for the quality of standing firm.
note.cn: 第一组是结构相似但指向不同对象的邻近短语；第二组是表示「站得稳」这一性质的词。

entries.definition: Soundness of government budgets and debt; it looks almost identical but concerns the treasury, not banks and markets.
entries.definitionCN: 指政府预算与债务的稳健；形式几乎相同，但关注国库，不是银行与市场。

entries.definition: A stable price level and currency, usually the target of interest-rate policy rather than of supervision.
entries.definitionCN: 指物价与币值稳定，通常是利率政策而非监管的目标。

entries.definition: Having enough money to live without fear; it applies to people, while financial stability applies to systems.
entries.definitionCN: 指有足够的钱生活而无忧；用于人，金融稳定则用于体系。

entries.definition: The body of rules governing finance; stability is the condition those rules aim at.
entries.definitionCN: 指治理金融的规则体系；稳定是这些规则想要达到的状态。

entries.definition: The quality of being financially healthy and well founded, often said of a bank or a currency.
entries.definitionCN: 指财务健康、基础牢靠，常用于银行或货币。

entries.definition: The capacity to absorb a shock and recover; stability is the state, resilience is the strength behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指承受冲击并恢复的能力；稳定是状态，韧性是背后的力量。

entries.definition: The quality of continuing to work under heavy strain, often used of systems and models.
entries.definitionCN: 指在重压下仍能运作的性质，常用于系统与模型。

entries.definition: A balance in which opposing forces cancel out; it is a theoretical state, not a supervisory goal.
entries.definitionCN: 指相互对抗的力量彼此抵消的平衡；是理论状态，不是监管目标。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Finance as the settling of debts plus stability as standing firm: a debt system that does not topple.
normal.cn: 金融是债务的结清，稳定是站得稳：一个不倒下的债务体系。

normal.en: The family runs finance, financial, stable, stability, stabilize and destabilize.
normal.cn: 同族词有 finance、financial、stable、stability、stabilize 与 destabilize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the policy sense: safeguard financial stability, threats to financial stability, the financial stability report.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出政策义：维护金融稳定、对金融稳定的威胁、金融稳定报告。

normal.en: Central banks pair it with supervision: stability is what supervision exists to protect.
normal.cn: 央行把它与监管配对：稳定正是监管所要守护的东西。

normal.en: The two halves come from different Latin words, one for an ending and one for standing.
normal.cn: 两半来自不同的拉丁词，一个指终点，一个指站立。

abstract.en: Picture a row of columns sharing one foundation, so none can settle without the others noticing.
abstract.cn: 想象一排柱子共享一个地基，任何一根下沉都会被其余察觉。

abstract.en: Picture a tightrope walker whose pole never tips past the point of no return.
abstract.cn: 想象一个走钢丝的人，长杆始终没有倾过不可挽回的那一点。

abstract.en: Picture a ship held level by many small corrections no passenger ever feels.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船靠许多乘客感觉不到的小修正保持水平。

examples.en: The committee meets quarterly to review financial stability risks.
examples.cn: 该委员会每季度开会审议金融稳定风险。

examples.en: Rapid credit growth can undermine financial stability.
examples.cn: 信贷快速增长可能损害金融稳定。

examples.en: Cross-border lending links the financial stability of both countries.
examples.cn: 跨境借贷把两国的金融稳定联结在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 一排柱子共享一个地基，没有一根开始倾斜 → 金融稳定

root: 英语复合短语：financial（出自拉丁 finis「终点」，经古法语指债务结清）+ stability（出自拉丁 stabilis「稳固」，再溯至 stare「站立」）；指金融体系不发生系统性危机的稳健状态。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one standing structure: the whole system, its institutions, market prices, household balance sheets, corporate balance sheets, the supervisory mandate, the cross-border layer, and the assessment that grades it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个「站稳的结构」：整个体系、其中的机构、市场价格、家庭资产负债表、企业资产负债表、监管职责、跨境层面，以及为它打分的评估。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: columns sharing one foundation, none of them beginning to tilt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排共享地基的柱子，没有一根开始倾斜。

branches.en: WHOLE STRUCTURE: the system is stable when it keeps standing through a shock.
branches.cn: 整体结构：体系在冲击下仍然站住，就是稳定。

branches.en: PARTS AND PRICES: banks and market prices are the visible members and signals of the same structure.
branches.cn: 成员与价格：银行与市场价格是同一结构可见的成员与信号。

branches.en: PRIVATE LAYERS: household and corporate balance sheets are lower floors that carry the structure.
branches.cn: 私人层面：家庭与企业资产负债表是承托这个结构的下面几层。

branches.en: DUTY: a condition worth keeping becomes a mandate once an authority is told to guard it.
branches.cn: 职责：值得守护的状态，在当局被指定守护之后成为职责。

branches.en: WIDER AND MEASURED: capital flows widen the structure, and assessment turns it into a score.
branches.cn: 更宽与可测：资本流动把这个结构拓宽，评估把它变成分数。

intro.en: Financial stability joins an ending word and a standing word, and both families build many English terms.
intro.cn: financial stability 由「终点」词与「站立」词合成，两个词族都构成不少英语术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis supplies finance, financial and final; Latin stare supplies stable, stability, stabilize and constant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 finis 给出 finance、financial 与 final；拉丁 stare 给出 stable、stability、stabilize 与 constant。

items.example: Settling a debt was seen as reaching an end.
items.exampleCN: 结清债务被看作走到一个终点。

items.example: The root pictures something that does not fall.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘不倒下的东西。

items.meaning: settlement of a payment; money management
items.example: The ministry manages public finance.
items.exampleCN: 该部管理公共财政。

items.example: The firm faced financial trouble.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司陷入财务困境。

items.example: Prices stayed stable through the year.
items.exampleCN: 全年价格保持稳定。

items.example: The stability of the currency reassured savers.
items.exampleCN: 货币的稳定让储户安心。

items.example: Rate cuts helped stabilize the market.
items.exampleCN: 降息帮助市场稳定下来。

items.example: Rumours destabilized the currency.
items.exampleCN: 传言使货币失去稳定。

definition_zh: 生意；商业；企业；行业；事务；职责；商务的
definition_en: the activity of buying and selling goods and services, a company that does this, or a matter that concerns someone
core_image: 一间临街铺面，卷帘门半开，柜台后面的人正把货递给顾客
scene: 镇上的面包房把小本生意做成了三家分店。The bakery in town turned a small business into three branches.
sceneCN: 镇上的面包房把小本生意做成了三家分店；句中的 business 指「以买卖为业的企业实体」（第 2 个义项：企业、商号）。图中可辨识物件：面包架、收银台、分店招牌、纸袋。

pos.zh: 生意；商业活动；企业；行业；事务；职责
商务的；营业的

derivatives.zh: 务实高效的；公事公办的

senses.title: Buying and selling as an activity
senses.definition: the activity of trading goods and services for money
senses.definitionCN: 以货物与服务换取金钱的活动
senses.example: Trade rules apply equally to all business conducted in the port.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易规则同样适用于港内进行的一切商业活动。
senses.why: The oldest sense is 'the state of being busy'; when what kept people busy was trade, the word came to name trade itself.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「忙碌的状态」；当人们忙的是买卖时，这个词就用来指买卖本身。

senses.title: A company that trades
senses.definition: a commercial organization that produces or sells goods and services
senses.definitionCN: 生产或销售货物与服务的商业组织
senses.example: The bakery in town turned a small business into three branches.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的面包房把小本生意做成了三家分店。
senses.why: An activity needs someone doing it, so the name of the activity moved onto the organization that carries it on.
senses.whyCN: 活动总要有人来做，于是活动的名称转移到承担它的组织上。

senses.title: A whole sector or field
senses.definition: a particular branch of trade, such as film, shipping or advertising
senses.definitionCN: 贸易的某一分支，如影视、航运或广告
senses.example: She has worked in the film business since college.
senses.exampleCN: 她从大学起就在影视行业工作。
senses.why: A field is a crowd of firms doing the same kind of trade, so the word widens from one firm to the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 一个领域是同做一类买卖的一大群企业，因此这个词从一家企业扩展到整个领域。

senses.title: A matter that concerns someone
senses.definition: a matter, concern or affair that belongs to a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 属于某人的事情、关切或事务
senses.example: What she does with her weekend is her own business.
senses.exampleCN: 她周末做什么是她自己的事。
senses.why: If being busy means having something to attend to, then business can mean simply the thing one has to attend to.
senses.whyCN: 如果忙碌意味着有事要处理，那么 business 就可以单纯指那个人要处理的事。

senses.title: The general state of trade
senses.definition: the level of trade and sales in a place or period
senses.definitionCN: 某地或某时期买卖与销售的兴旺程度
senses.example: Business is slow in the weeks after the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 假期之后的几周里生意清淡。
senses.why: Counting all the busy trading together produces a general condition, which is neither one firm nor one activity.
senses.whyCN: 把所有忙碌的买卖合起来看，就得到一种总体状况，既不是某家企业，也不是某笔活动。

senses.title: Commercial relations with a partner
senses.definition: the commercial relationship or custom that a person or firm has with another
senses.definitionCN: 个人或企业与他方建立的商业关系或客户往来
senses.example: We have done business with that supplier for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 我们与那家供应商做了十年生意。
senses.why: Trade is not a single act but a repeating relation, and the word names that continuing connection.
senses.whyCN: 买卖不是一次性动作，而是反复发生的关系，这个词就用来指这种持续的联结。

senses.title: Used before a noun: commercial or working
senses.definition: placed before a noun to mean connected with trade or with the working side of an organization
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示与买卖或机构的工作层面有关
senses.example: The shop has shortened its business hours since spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店从春天起缩短了营业时间。
senses.why: The attributive use lets the noun act as a label, marking a trip, a district or an hour as belonging to trade.
senses.whyCN: 定语用法让这个名词充当标签，把出行、区域或时段标记为属于买卖。

senses.title: The serious matter at hand
senses.titleCN: 正事；手头该处理的议程
senses.definition: the serious work or topic that is waiting to be dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 等着被处理的正经工作或议题
senses.example: After the introductions, the committee got down to business.
senses.exampleCN: 介绍过后，委员会开始谈正事。
senses.why: The sense of a matter to attend to narrows to the one matter that must be attended to now.
senses.whyCN: 「有待处理的事」这一义收窄为此刻必须处理的那件事。

intro.en: Business is an English noun built on busy, from Old English bisig 'occupied, diligent'. It first meant the state of being busy, then the matters that kept one busy, and only later trade. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: business 是英语本族名词，由 busy 构成，源自古英语 bisig「忙碌的、勤勉的」。它最初指忙碌的状态，继而指使人忙碌的事务，后来才指买卖。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bisig meant 'busy, occupied, diligent', and its deeper origin is not established; it may be related to Dutch bezig, but that link is not proved.
items.cn: bisig 意为「忙碌的、有事在身的、勤勉的」，其更深来源未有定论；可能与荷兰语 bezig 有关，但这一联系未获证明。

items.en: The suffix -ness turned the adjective into a noun of state, so business first meant simply 'busyness'.
items.cn: 后缀 -ness 把形容词变成表示状态的名词，因此 business 最初只表示「忙碌」。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the word had shifted from the state to the things that caused it: affairs, concerns and duties.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，这个词从状态转向造成状态的事物：事务、关切与职责。

items.en: In the seventeenth century commerce became the dominant kind of busy affair, and business took over as the general word for trade.
items.cn: 十七世纪，商业成为最主要的「忙碌事务」，business 遂成为买卖的通用词。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-English origin of bisig is unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定：bisig 在英语之前的历史没有定论，凡为其给出的更早形式都属重构形式，而非有记录的词。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound like business but name a state, a manner or a person; group two holds words for trade as a whole.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近、但指状态、方式或人的词；第二组是整体指买卖的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning occupied with activity; business is the noun made from it, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指忙于活动的形容词；business 是由它构成的名词，二者不是同义词。

entries.definition: The literal state of being busy; it keeps the older meaning that business has largely left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 字面上「忙碌的状态」；保留了 business 大体已经放弃的旧义。

entries.definition: An adjective for doing things efficiently and without fuss, describing a style rather than an enterprise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指做事高效、不拖泥带水，描述风格而非企业。

entries.definition: A man engaged in trade; the compound narrows the field to one person.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事买卖的男子；这个复合词把范围收窄到一个人。

entries.definition: Trade between regions or nations, especially in bulk; more formal and wider in scope than business.
entries.definitionCN: 指地区或国家之间、尤其大宗贸易，比 business 更正式、范围更广。

entries.definition: The exchange of goods, or a particular line of it; it stresses the swap rather than the organization.
entries.definitionCN: 指货物的交换或某一行当；强调交换本身，而非组织。

entries.definition: The organized production of goods, or a branch of it; it begins at the making, not the selling.
entries.definitionCN: 指有组织的生产或其中一门类；起点在制造，不在销售。

entries.definition: A bold undertaking or a firm, with a tone of initiative; business is the plainer, broader word.
entries.definitionCN: 指大胆的事业或企业，带进取意味；business 是更平实宽泛的词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Busy plus the state suffix: first the state of being occupied, then the affairs that occupy one, then trade.
normal.cn: 「忙碌」加状态后缀：先指忙碌的状态，再指占用人时间的事务，最后指买卖。

normal.en: The family runs business, businesses, businessman, businesswoman and businesslike.
normal.cn: 同族词有 business、businesses、businessman、businesswoman 与 businesslike。

normal.en: Fixed phrases cover the everyday senses: do business with, business hours, none of your business, get down to business.
normal.cn: 固定说法覆盖日常各义：与某人做生意、营业时间、不关你的事、开始谈正事。

normal.en: The plural businesses counts firms, not activities.
normal.cn: 复数 businesses 数的是企业，不是活动。

normal.en: The same stem gives busy and busyness, which keep the older meaning.
normal.cn: 同一词干给出 busy 与 busyness，它们保留了更早的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a shop door half open, with a queue that never quite empties.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇半开的店门，门外队伍始终没有完全散尽。

abstract.en: Picture a desk covered in papers, each one a matter waiting to be dealt with.
abstract.cn: 想象一张堆满文件的桌子，每份文件都是一件待处理的事。

abstract.en: Picture a single stall that quietly grows into a row of stalls along the same street.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摊位悄悄长成同一条街上的一排摊位。

examples.en: Small businesses in the district received a tax credit this year.
examples.cn: 本区的小企业今年获得了税收抵免。

examples.en: She runs a catering business from her own kitchen.
examples.cn: 她用自己的厨房经营一家餐饮企业。

examples.en: It is not my business to judge how they spend the money.
examples.cn: 评判他们怎么花这笔钱不关我的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 铺面半开，货物不断递过柜台，门外还排着队 → 生意

root: 英语本族词：busy（古英语 bisig「忙碌的、勤勉的」）+ 状态后缀 -ness；由「忙碌状态」引申为「事务」，再引申为「买卖、企业」。bisig 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one stem: the activity of trade, the firm that carries it on, the whole field, a personal affair, the general state of trade, a continuing commercial relation, the attributive label, and the serious matter at hand.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个词干展开：买卖活动、承担它的企业、整个行业、个人事务、商业总体状况、持续的业务关系、定语标签，以及手头的正事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shop counter with goods passing across it and a queue outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张柜台，货物从上面递过，门外还排着队。

branches.en: ACTIVITY: what keeps people busy becomes the name of the trading itself.
branches.cn: 活动：使人忙碌的事，变成买卖本身的名称。

branches.en: SCALE: one firm and one whole field are the same trade seen at two sizes.
branches.cn: 尺度：一家企业与整个行业，是同一行当的两种大小。

branches.en: AFFAIR: a private matter and the matter at hand are both things that occupy a person.
branches.cn: 事务：私事与手头的事，都是占用人注意力的事。

branches.en: CONDITION: adding up all the trading produces a general state of busyness.
branches.cn: 状况：把所有买卖加起来，得到一种总体忙碌状况。

branches.en: RELATION AND LABEL: repeated dealing becomes a relationship, and the noun turns into a marker before other nouns.
branches.cn: 关系与标签：反复往来成为关系，名词也变成其他名词前的标记。

intro.en: Business is a native English construction from an adjective plus a state suffix, so its parts are plain and its family is large.
intro.cn: business 是英语本族构词，由一个形容词加状态后缀构成，成分朴素，词族庞大。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin root; its nearest neighbours are the English adjective busy and the suffix -ness.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根；最近的邻居是英语形容词 busy 与后缀 -ness。

items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a state noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成状态名词。

items.example: The business grew into three branches.
items.exampleCN: 这家企业发展成三家分店。

items.example: Three businesses share the building.
items.exampleCN: 三家企业在同一栋楼里。

items.example: Her businesslike reply ended the debate.
items.exampleCN: 她公事公办的回答结束了争论。

items.example: The businessman checked his watch.
items.exampleCN: 那位商人看了看表。

items.example: The businesswoman led the negotiation.
items.exampleCN: 那位女商人主导了谈判。

items.example: Busyness is not the same as progress.
items.exampleCN: 忙碌并不等于进展。

derivatives.zh: 务实高效的；公事公办的

definition_zh: 商人；企业家；男性商务人士
definition_en: a man who works in business, especially one who owns or runs a company
core_image: 谈判桌一端，一个穿灰西装的男人边看表边把报价单往对面推
scene: 谈判桌上，那位穿灰西装的男人一边看表一边压价。At the negotiating table, the businessman in the grey suit kept checking his watch while pushing the price down.
sceneCN: 谈判桌上，那位穿灰西装的男人一边看表一边压价；句中的 businessman 指「以经营企业为职业的男性」（第 1 个义项：经商的男性）。图中可辨识物件：皮公文包、报价单、腕表、会议桌。

pos.zh: 商人；企业家；男性商务人士

senses.title: A man who works in trade
senses.definition: a man whose occupation is buying and selling or managing commercial affairs
senses.definitionCN: 以买卖或处理商业事务为职业的男子
senses.example: At the negotiating table, the businessman in the grey suit kept checking his watch while pushing the price down.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判桌上，那位穿灰西装的男人一边看表一边压价。
senses.why: The compound simply joins the name of trade to the word for a man, so its first sense is the plain sum of its parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词只是把买卖的名称与「男人」一词连在一起，最初的意思就是两部分的直接相加。

senses.title: The owner of a firm, not just its employee
senses.definition: a man who owns or controls a company, especially a family firm or a private enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或掌控一家公司，尤指家族企业或私营企业的男子
senses.example: The businessman sold his chain of garages to a rival group.
senses.exampleCN: 这位企业主把连锁修车厂卖给了竞争对手。
senses.why: Ownership is the oldest and strongest form of having business, so the word leans towards the person whose name is over the door.
senses.whyCN: 所有权是最古老也最有力的「有生意」，因此这个词偏向门口挂着他名字的人。

senses.title: A senior commercial executive
senses.definition: a man in a senior managerial position who represents a company in negotiations or public life
senses.definitionCN: 担任高级管理职务、代表公司参与谈判或公共活动的男子
senses.example: Several businessmen accompanied the trade mission abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 几位商业高管随贸易代表团出访。
senses.why: As companies grew, the man who spoke for one at a table became a businessman even without owning it.
senses.whyCN: 随着公司变大，在桌边代表公司说话的人，即使不拥有这家公司，也被称为 businessman。

senses.title: A man who has founded something
senses.titleCN: 男性创业者；创业的企业人
senses.definition: a man who has started and built a commercial venture, often from little
senses.definitionCN: 白手起步、创立并发展一项商业事业的男子
senses.example: The businessman started with one van and ended with forty.
senses.exampleCN: 这位创业者从一辆货车起家，最后拥有四十辆。
senses.why: Building a firm is business in its most active form, so the person who builds one fits the word naturally.
senses.whyCN: 把企业建起来是「生意」最活跃的形态，因此建企业的人自然适配这个词。

senses.title: A hard bargainer
senses.definition: a man known for driving a hard bargain and watching costs closely
senses.definitionCN: 以压价狠、盯成本紧而出名的男子
senses.example: He is too much of a businessman to accept the first offer.
senses.exampleCN: 他太像个商人了，不会接受第一份报价。
senses.why: The word carries the market's habits, and a reputation for sharp dealing is one of the traits it names.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着市场的习性，而「做买卖很精」正是它所命名的特质之一。

senses.title: A man travelling for work
senses.definition: a man away from home on company business, especially in hotels and airports
senses.definitionCN: 因公离家外出的男子，常见于酒店与机场
senses.example: The lounge was full of businessmen waiting for the evening flight.
senses.exampleCN: 休息室里挤满了等晚班航班的商务旅客。
senses.why: Modern travel separated the trader from his shop, and the same word came to describe the man on the move for trade.
senses.whyCN: 现代出行把商人从他的店铺分开，同一个词于是也用来描述为生意在路上的人。

senses.title: A man seen as caring only about profit
senses.definition: used disapprovingly of a man thought to value profit above people or principles
senses.definitionCN: 贬义用法，指被认为把利润置于人之上、压倒原则的男子
senses.example: Critics dismissed the plan as the work of businessmen, not doctors.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者轻蔑地说这是唯利是图者的方案，不是医生的方案。
senses.why: A word that names trade can also carry suspicion of trade, and this pejorative shade is part of its history.
senses.whyCN: 命名买卖的词也可能带上对买卖的疑心，这层贬义是它历史的一部分。

senses.title: A representative of the business community
senses.definition: a man who speaks for commerce in public bodies, chambers or delegations
senses.definitionCN: 在公共机构、商会或代表团中代表商界发言的男子
senses.example: The chamber invited two businessmen to advise the transport committee.
senses.exampleCN: 商会请了两位商界代表为交通委员会提供意见。
senses.why: Once business organizes into chambers and lobbies, its members become public representatives of a sector.
senses.whyCN: 当商界组织成商会与游说团体，其成员就成为某个行业的公共代表。

intro.en: Businessman is an English compound of business and man, recorded from the nineteenth century. An older phrase, man of business, meant an agent who handled another person's affairs. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: businessman 是英语复合词，由 business 与 man 构成，十九世纪起有记录。更早的说法「办事代理人」指替他人处理事务的人。年代均为约数。

items.en: The earlier phrase man of business named an agent or steward who managed another person's affairs, not a trader in his own right.
items.cn: 更早的说法「办事之人」指代理或管家，替别人处理事务，并不是自己做买卖的人。

items.en: As trade expanded and firms grew, English joined the two nouns directly into businessman, naming the man whose work was business.
items.cn: 随着贸易扩张与企业成长，英语把这两个名词直接合成 businessman，指以商业为业的人。

items.en: Man descends from Old English mann, 'person, human being', so the second element originally meant a person rather than specifically a male.
items.cn: man 源自古英语 mann「人、人类」，因此第二部分原本指一个人，而不专指男性。

items.en: Businesswoman appeared as a parallel form when women entered commerce in large numbers, and both compounds stayed in use.
items.cn: 当大量女性进入商界，businesswoman 作为并列形式出现，两个复合词都沿用下来。

items.en: In official writing the gender-neutral business person has partly replaced both, especially where the sex of the person is irrelevant.
items.cn: 在正式文书里，中性的「商务人士」说法部分取代了两者，尤其在人别无所谓时。

note.en: Group one holds compounds built on the same first element; group two holds other names for people in trade.
note.cn: 第一组是同一前半部分构成的复合词；第二组是商界中人的其他称呼。

entries.definition: The trade itself or the firm; businessman adds the person who carries it on.
entries.definitionCN: 指买卖本身或企业；businessman 加上的是从事它的人。

entries.definition: The same compound with woman; the senses match one by one, only the sex differs.
entries.definitionCN: 同一复合词换用「女人」；各义项一一对应，只差性别。

entries.definition: The gender-neutral phrase used in formal writing for anyone in trade.
entries.definitionCN: 正式文书中的中性说法，指商界中的任何人。

entries.definition: An adjective for efficient, practical behaviour; it describes manner, never a person's occupation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指高效务实的行为；描述做事方式，不指职业。

entries.definition: Someone who trades in goods, often across distances; older and more specific than businessman.
entries.definitionCN: 指买卖货物的人，常涉及远距离贸易；比 businessman 更古老、更具体。

entries.definition: A person who buys and sells, especially in markets or financial instruments; narrower in activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指在市场上或金融工具上买卖的人；活动范围更窄。

entries.definition: A senior manager in an organization; businessman may own a firm, while an executive usually does not.
entries.definitionCN: 指组织中的高级管理者；businessman 可能是企业主，executive 通常不是。

entries.definition: Someone who starts a venture and bears the risk; businessman is the broader, older label.
entries.definitionCN: 指创立事业并承担风险的人；businessman 是更宽、更旧的称呼。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Business plus man: the trade and the person who carries it on.
normal.cn: 「生意」加「男人」：买卖与从事买卖的人。

normal.en: The plural is businessmen, not businessmans.
normal.cn: 复数是不规则形式 businessmen，不是 businessmans。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: a local businessman, a wealthy businessman, a retired businessman.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：本地商人、富商、退休商人。

normal.en: The earlier phrase man of business meant an agent, which explains the managerial shade.
normal.cn: 更早的说法「办事之人」指代理人，这解释了管理层的含义。

normal.en: The neutral replacement is business person.
normal.cn: 中性替代说法是「商务人士」。

abstract.en: Picture a man with two watches, one for the meeting and one for the market.
abstract.cn: 想象一个戴两块表的男人，一块看会议，一块看行情。

abstract.en: Picture a briefcase that opens into a whole shop counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只公文包打开就变成整张柜台。

abstract.en: Picture a name painted above a door, and the man standing under it.
abstract.cn: 想象门楣上刷着一个名字，名字下站着那个人。

examples.en: A local businessman donated the land for the clinic.
examples.cn: 一位本地商人捐出了建诊所的土地。

examples.en: The businessman flew to three cities in one week.
examples.cn: 这位商人一周飞了三个城市。

examples.en: She married a retired businessman who now runs a small vineyard.
examples.cn: 她嫁给了一位退休商人，他现在经营一座小葡萄园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谈判桌旁穿灰西装、腕上带表的男人 → 商人

root: 英语复合词：business（古英语 bisig「忙碌」加状态后缀）+ man（古英语 mann「人」）；十九世纪起指以商业为业的人，更早的说法指替人办事的代理。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one man at the table: the trader, the owner, the executive, the founder, the hard bargainer, the traveller, the profit-only caricature, and the sector's public representative.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕谈判桌旁的一个人：经商的男子、企业主、高管、创业者、压价能手、出差者、只重利益的漫画形象，以及商界的公共代表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man in a grey suit at a negotiating table, watch on wrist, offer on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：谈判桌旁一位穿灰西装的男子，腕上有表，桌上摆着报价单。

branches.en: MAN IN TRADE: the compound's plain sum, a person whose work is buying and selling.
branches.cn: 经商的男子：复合词的字面相加，以买卖为业的人。

branches.en: OWNER AND FOUNDER: holding the firm and having built it are two ways of being the man behind the door.
branches.cn: 业主与创始人：拥有这家企业与把它建起来，是「门后那个人」的两种形态。

branches.en: SPOKESMAN: speaking for a firm at a table grows into speaking for a whole sector.
branches.cn: 代言者：在桌边代表一家企业，进而代表整个行业。

branches.en: MARKET HABIT: sharp dealing is the word's characteristic behaviour rather than a job title.
branches.cn: 市场习性：精于压价是这个词的典型行为，而非职位。

branches.en: AWAY AND SUSPECT: travel separates him from the shop, and suspicion of profit colours the name.
branches.cn: 在外与被疑：出行把他与店铺分开，对利润的疑心又给这个名字上色。

intro.en: Businessman is a transparent English compound; each half keeps its own family and the plural changes the second element.
intro.cn: businessman 是结构透明的英语复合词；两半各自保留词族，复数只改后半部分。

latinIntro.en: Neither half has a Latin root: business comes from an Old English adjective, man from Old English mann.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都没有拉丁词根：business 出自古英语形容词，man 出自古英语 mann。

items.example: The business grew quickly.
items.exampleCN: 这家企业发展得很快。

items.example: The man at the counter knew every customer.
items.exampleCN: 柜台后的人认识每位顾客。

items.example: The businessman pushed the price down.
items.exampleCN: 那位商人把价格压了下去。

items.example: Two businessmen joined the mission.
items.exampleCN: 两位商人加入了代表团。

items.example: The businessman's office overlooks the harbour.
items.exampleCN: 这位商人的办公室俯瞰港口。

items.example: The businesswoman closed the deal.
items.exampleCN: 那位女商人完成了交易。

items.meaning: neutral term for a person in trade
items.example: Each business person received a badge.
items.exampleCN: 每位商务人士都领到一枚胸牌。

items.example: He answered in a businesslike way.
items.exampleCN: 他以公事公办的方式回答。

definition_en: a woman who works in business, especially one who owns or runs a company

sceneCN: 会议开始前，她把三份合同摊在桌上逐条核对；句中的 businesswoman 指「以经营企业为职业的女性」（第 1 个义项：经商的女性）。图中可辨识物件：合同夹、签字笔、会议桌、胸牌。

pos.zh: 女商人；女企业家；女性商务人士

derivatives.zh: 具有女商人作风的（少用）

senses.title: A woman who works in trade
senses.definition: a woman whose occupation is buying and selling or managing commercial affairs
senses.definitionCN: 以买卖或处理商业事务为职业的女性
senses.example: Before the meeting began, the businesswoman spread three contracts across the table and checked each clause.
senses.exampleCN: 会议开始前，她把三份合同摊在桌上逐条核对。
senses.why: The compound joins the name of trade to the word for a woman, so its first sense is simply the sum of its two parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把买卖的名称与「女人」一词连在一起，最初的意思就是两部分的直接相加。

senses.title: The owner of a firm
senses.definition: a woman who owns or controls a company, especially a family firm or a private business
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或掌控一家公司，尤指家族企业或私营企业的女性
senses.example: The businesswoman sold the family bakery after thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位女企业主在三十年后卖掉了家族面包房。
senses.why: Ownership is the strongest form of having business, so the word leans towards the woman whose name is over the door.
senses.whyCN: 所有权是最有力的「有生意」，因此这个词偏向门口挂着她名字的人。

senses.title: A senior commercial executive
senses.definition: a woman in a senior managerial position who represents a company in negotiations or public life
senses.definitionCN: 担任高级管理职务、代表公司参与谈判或公共活动的女性
senses.example: The businesswoman chaired the trade delegation to the north.
senses.exampleCN: 这位女高管主持了前往北方的贸易代表团。
senses.why: As firms grew, the person who spoke for one at a table counted as a businesswoman even without owning it.
senses.whyCN: 随着企业变大，在桌边代表企业说话的人，即使不拥有它，也算作女商人。

senses.title: A woman who has founded something
senses.definition: a woman who has started and built a commercial venture, often from little
senses.definitionCN: 白手起步、创立并发展一项商业事业的女性
senses.example: The businesswoman began with one sewing machine and now employs forty people.
senses.exampleCN: 这位创业者从一台缝纫机起家，如今雇了四十人。
senses.why: Building a firm is business in its most active form, so the person who builds one fits the word naturally.
senses.whyCN: 把企业建起来是「生意」最活跃的形态，因此建企业的人自然适配这个词。

senses.title: A hard bargainer
senses.definition: a woman known for driving a hard bargain and watching costs closely
senses.definitionCN: 以压价狠、盯成本紧而出名的女性
senses.example: She is too much of a businesswoman to accept the first offer.
senses.exampleCN: 她太像个做生意的了，不会接受第一份报价。
senses.why: The word carries the market's habits, and a reputation for sharp dealing is one of the traits it names.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着市场的习性，而「做买卖很精」正是它所命名的特质之一。

senses.title: A woman travelling for work
senses.definition: a woman away from home on company business, especially in hotels and airports
senses.definitionCN: 因公离家外出的女性，常见于酒店与机场
senses.example: The lounge was full of businesswomen waiting for the morning flight.
senses.exampleCN: 休息室里挤满了等早班航班的女商务旅客。
senses.why: Modern travel separated the trader from her shop, and the word came to describe the woman on the move for trade.
senses.whyCN: 现代出行把商人从她的店铺分开，这个词于是也用来描述为生意在路上的女性。

senses.title: A woman seen as caring only about profit
senses.definition: used disapprovingly of a woman thought to value profit above people or principles
senses.definitionCN: 贬义用法，指被认为把利润置于人之上、压倒原则的女性
senses.example: The column attacked her as a businesswoman with no interest in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇专栏攻击她只是个唯利是图的商人，对本镇毫无关心。
senses.why: A word that names trade can carry suspicion of trade, and this pejorative shade belongs to its history.
senses.whyCN: 命名买卖的词也可能带上对买卖的疑心，这层贬义属于它的历史。

senses.title: A representative of the business community
senses.definition: a woman who speaks for commerce in public bodies, chambers or delegations
senses.definitionCN: 在公共机构、商会或代表团中代表商界发言的女性
senses.example: The chamber invited a businesswoman to advise the housing committee.
senses.exampleCN: 商会请了一位商界女性代表为住房委员会提供意见。
senses.why: Once business organizes into chambers and lobbies, its members become public representatives of a sector.
senses.whyCN: 当商界组织成商会与游说团体，其成员就成为某个行业的公共代表。

intro.en: Businesswoman is an English compound of business and woman, recorded from the nineteenth century, when women entered trade in growing numbers. An older phrase, woman of business, meant a woman who handled practical affairs. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: businesswoman 是英语复合词，由 business 与 woman 构成，十九世纪起有记录，当时女性进入商界的人数不断增加。更早的说法「办事的女人」指处理实务的女性。年代均为约数。

items.en: The earlier phrase woman of business described a woman who managed practical affairs, often for a household or an estate.
items.cn: 更早的说法「办事的女人」指管理实务的女性，常是为家庭或产业办事。

items.en: As shops, offices and firms multiplied, English joined the two nouns into businesswoman, naming the woman whose work was business.
items.cn: 随着店铺、事务所与企业增多，英语把这两个名词合成 businesswoman，指以商业为业的女人。

items.en: Woman descends from Old English wifmann, originally 'female person', built from wif 'female' and mann 'person'.
items.cn: woman 源自古英语 wifmann，原意是「女性的人」，由 wif「女性」与 mann「人」构成。

items.en: Businessman was the older default, and businesswoman arose as its exact parallel rather than as a separate word with its own senses.
items.cn: businessman 原本是默认说法，businesswoman 是作为它完全对应的形式出现的，并非另有一套义项的词。

items.en: In official writing the neutral business person is often preferred, especially where the sex of the person is irrelevant.
items.cn: 在正式文书里，中性的「商务人士」常被优先使用，尤其在人别无所谓时。

note.en: Group one holds compounds built on the same first element; group two holds other names for women or people in trade.
note.cn: 第一组是同一前半部分构成的复合词；第二组是商界女性的其他称呼。

entries.definition: The same compound with man; the senses match one by one, only the sex differs.
entries.definitionCN: 同一复合词换用「男人」；各义项一一对应，只差性别。

entries.definition: The trade itself or the firm; businesswoman adds the person who carries it on.
entries.definitionCN: 指买卖本身或企业；businesswoman 加上的是从事它的人。

entries.definition: The possessive, meaning belonging to such a woman; it is a form, not a separate sense.
entries.definitionCN: 所有格形式，表示属于这样的女性；它只是形式，不是独立义项。

entries.definition: The gender-neutral phrase used in formal writing for anyone in trade.
entries.definitionCN: 正式文书中的中性说法，指商界中的任何人。

entries.definition: Someone who trades in goods, often across distances; older and more specific than businesswoman.
entries.definitionCN: 指买卖货物的人，常涉及远距离贸易；比 businesswoman 更古老、更具体。

entries.definition: A senior manager in an organization; a businesswoman may own a firm, while an executive usually does not.
entries.definitionCN: 指组织中的高级管理者；女商人可能是企业主，executive 通常不是。

entries.definition: Someone who starts a venture and bears the risk; businesswoman is the broader, older label.
entries.definitionCN: 指创立事业并承担风险的人；businesswoman 是更宽、更旧的称呼。

entries.definition: The legal owner of a business or property; it states ownership, not the everyday role.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业或财产的法定所有人；它陈述所有权，不指日常角色。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Business plus woman: the trade and the person who carries it on.
normal.cn: 「生意」加「女人」：买卖与从事买卖的人。

normal.en: The plural is businesswomen, not businesswomans.
normal.cn: 复数是不规则形式 businesswomen，不是 businesswomans。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: a local businesswoman, a wealthy businesswoman, a retired businesswoman.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：本地女商人、富有的女商人、退休的女商人。

normal.en: Woman itself came from a compound meaning 'female person', so the word is a compound inside a compound.
normal.cn: woman 本身来自意为「女性的人」的复合词，因此这个词是复合词里再套复合词。

normal.en: The neutral replacement is business person.
normal.cn: 中性替代说法是「商务人士」。

abstract.en: Picture three contracts laid side by side, each clause underlined in a different colour.
abstract.cn: 想象三份合同并排摊开，每一条款都用不同颜色的笔划过。

abstract.en: Picture a name plate on a door that was repainted rather than replaced.
abstract.cn: 想象门上的名牌是重新刷漆的，而不是换掉的。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger held open by one hand while the other hand shakes another.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按住摊开的账本，另一只手与人相握。

examples.en: A local businesswoman funded the new library wing.
examples.cn: 一位本地女商人出资建了图书馆的新侧厅。

examples.en: The businesswoman flew to two countries in a single week.
examples.cn: 这位女商人一周内飞了两个国家。

examples.en: The committee heard from a businesswoman who runs a chain of nurseries.
examples.cn: 委员会听取了一位经营连锁托儿所的女商人的意见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 会议桌前把合同逐条摊开核对的女性 → 女商人

root: 英语复合词：business（古英语 bisig「忙碌」加状态后缀）+ woman（古英语 wifmann「女性的人」）；十九世纪起指以商业为业的女人。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one woman at the table: the trader, the owner, the executive, the founder, the hard bargainer, the traveller, the profit-only caricature, and the sector's public representative.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕会议桌旁的一位女性：经商的女子、企业主、高管、创业者、压价能手、出差者、只重利益的漫画形象，以及商界的公共代表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a woman at a meeting table with three contracts laid out before her.
core.cn: 核心意象：会议桌旁一位女性，面前摊着三份合同。

branches.en: WOMAN IN TRADE: the compound's plain sum, a person whose work is buying and selling.
branches.cn: 经商的女子：复合词的字面相加，以买卖为业的人。

branches.en: OWNER AND FOUNDER: holding the firm and having built it are two ways of being the woman behind the door.
branches.cn: 业主与创始人：拥有这家企业与把它建起来，是「门后那个人」的两种形态。

branches.en: SPOKESPERSON: speaking for a firm at a table grows into speaking for a whole sector.
branches.cn: 代言者：在桌边代表一家企业，进而代表整个行业。

branches.en: MARKET HABIT: sharp dealing is the word's characteristic behaviour rather than a job title.
branches.cn: 市场习性：精于压价是这个词的典型行为，而非职位。

branches.en: AWAY AND SUSPECT: travel separates her from the shop, and suspicion of profit colours the name.
branches.cn: 在外与被疑：出行把她与店铺分开，对利润的疑心又给这个名字上色。

intro.en: Businesswoman is a transparent English compound; each half keeps its own family and the plural changes the second element.
intro.cn: businesswoman 是结构透明的英语复合词；两半各自保留词族，复数只改后半部分。

latinIntro.en: Neither half has a Latin root: business comes from an Old English adjective, woman from an Old English compound for a female person.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都没有拉丁词根：business 出自古英语形容词，woman 出自古英语中表示「女性的人」的复合词。

items.exampleCN: 桌边的那位女士处理合同。

items.example: The businesswoman checked each clause.
items.exampleCN: 那位女商人逐条核对了条款。

items.example: Three businesswomen joined the chamber.
items.exampleCN: 三位女商人加入了商会。

items.example: The businesswoman's firm opened a branch.
items.exampleCN: 这位女商人的公司开了一家分店。

items.example: The businessman sat opposite her.
items.exampleCN: 那位男商人坐在她对面。

items.meaning: neutral term for a person in trade
items.example: Each business person received a badge.
items.exampleCN: 每位商务人士都领到一枚胸牌。

items.example: She gave a businesslike reply.
items.exampleCN: 她公事公办地回答。

definition_zh: 企业；事业；计划；进取心；经营；私营企业体系
definition_en: a company or business, a bold or difficult undertaking, or the drive to start and run ventures
core_image: 一间小厂房里，几个人围着一张图纸，把第一台机器推上地基
scene: 这家做水质监测的小公司去年拿到了海外订单。The small enterprise that monitors water quality won an overseas order last year.
sceneCN: 这家做水质监测的小公司去年拿到了海外订单；句中的 enterprise 指「从事经营的企业实体」（第 1 个义项：企业、商业组织）。图中可辨识物件：水质检测仪、厂房、订单文件、工具箱。

pos.zh: 企业；事业；计划；进取心；经营
创业精神；开拓进取
