senses.title: A commercial organization
senses.definition: a company or business organization, especially one that produces goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 生产货物或提供服务的企业或商业组织
senses.example: The small enterprise that monitors water quality won an overseas order last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家做水质监测的小公司去年拿到了海外订单。
senses.why: The word began as 'something undertaken', and a firm is precisely something a group of people undertakes together.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「被承担起来的事」，而企业正是一群人共同承担起来的那件事。

senses.title: A bold or difficult undertaking
senses.titleCN: 大胆或艰难的事业、计划
senses.definition: a large or risky project that requires effort and courage to carry through
senses.definitionCN: 需要付出与勇气才能完成的大型或有风险的项目
senses.example: Mapping the whole cave system was a dangerous enterprise.
senses.exampleCN: 测绘整个洞穴系统是一项危险的事业。
senses.why: Undertaking something is the oldest sense: the word names the thing taken on before it names the firm that takes it on.
senses.whyCN: 「承担某件事」是最古老的意思：这个词先命名被承担的事，再命名承担它的企业。

senses.title: The drive to start things
senses.definition: the quality of initiative and willingness to start new ventures
senses.definitionCN: 主动开创、愿意启动新事业的性质
senses.example: The prize rewards enterprise among young farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个奖项奖励年轻农场主中的进取精神。
senses.why: If an enterprise is something undertaken, the willingness to undertake things can carry the same name.
senses.whyCN: 如果 enterprise 是被承担的事，那么愿意承担事情的意愿也能用同一个名称。

senses.title: Business activity in general
senses.definition: commercial activity, especially the conduct of trade by private parties
senses.definitionCN: 商业活动，尤指私人方面从事的买卖
senses.example: The law protects enterprise and discourages monopoly.
senses.exampleCN: 法律保护经营活动，抑制垄断。
senses.why: The activity of undertaking ventures became a general name for doing business at all.
senses.whyCN: 承担事业的这种活动，变成了泛指「做买卖」的名称。

senses.title: The private business system
senses.titleCN: 私营企业体系；自由企业制度
senses.definition: the system in which private owners, rather than the state, run businesses
senses.definitionCN: 由私人而非国家经营企业的制度
senses.example: Free enterprise is credited with the region's rapid growth.
senses.exampleCN: 人们把该地区的快速增长归功于自由企业制度。
senses.why: When private ventures are treated as a system, the word moves from one firm to the whole order that allows firms.
senses.whyCN: 当私人事业被当作一套制度来看，这个词就从一家企业扩展到允许企业存在的整个秩序。

senses.title: A large engineering or public project
senses.definition: a big construction or infrastructure project, often public and long-running
senses.definitionCN: 大型建设或基础设施项目，常为公共且耗时较久
senses.example: The dam was the largest enterprise the province had attempted.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大坝是该省尝试过的最大的工程。
senses.why: Public works are undertakings too, so the word keeps its older project sense alongside the commercial one.
senses.whyCN: 公共工程也是「被承担的事」，因此这个词在商业义之外保留了较旧的项目义。

senses.title: A state-owned or public firm
senses.definition: a business owned by the state or a public body, as opposed to a private company
senses.definitionCN: 由国家或公共机构拥有的企业，与私营公司相对
senses.example: The state enterprise controls the northern rail link.
senses.exampleCN: 这家国有企业控制着北部铁路线。
senses.why: Once states began to own firms, the same noun needed a modifier, and the modifier became part of the name.
senses.whyCN: 当国家开始拥有企业，同一个名词就需要修饰语，修饰语随后成为名称的一部分。

senses.title: A firm with a social purpose
senses.definition: a business that trades to pursue a social or environmental mission rather than to maximize profit
senses.definitionCN: 以社会或环境使命而非利润最大化为目的进行经营的企业
senses.example: The enterprise trains unemployed teenagers to repair bicycles.
senses.exampleCN: 这家社会企业培训失业青少年修理自行车。
senses.why: The undertaking sense returns in a new form: what is undertaken is not profit but a public good.
senses.whyCN: 「承担之事」的意思以新形态回归：被承担的不是利润，而是公共利益。

intro.en: Enterprise comes through Old French entreprise 'something undertaken' from entreprendre 'to take in hand, undertake', built on entre- 'between' and prendre 'to take'. Its commercial sense is much later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: enterprise 经古法语 entreprise「被承担起来的事」来自 entreprendre「着手、承担」，由 entre-「之间」与 prendre「拿取」构成。它的商业义出现得晚得多。年代均为约数。

items.en: Prehendere meant 'to seize, grasp, take hold of', and its past participle prehensus underlies the French verb for taking something in hand.
items.cn: prehendere 意为「抓住、握取、拿住」，其过去分词 prehensus 是法语中「着手拿住」这一动词的基础。

items.en: Entreprendre joined a prefix meaning 'between, among' to the verb for taking, giving 'to take in hand, begin, undertake'.
items.cn: entreprendre 把意为「之间、其中」的前缀与「拿取」的动词结合，得到「着手、开始、承担」。

items.en: English borrowed enterprise for a venture or an undertaking, often a military or building project, with no commercial colour at first.
items.cn: 英语借入 enterprise 指一项冒险或事业，常为军事或建筑工程，起初没有商业色彩。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries the word shifted towards business activity and the firm that conducts it, and the older project sense survived beside it.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪，这个词转向商业活动与从事商业的企业，较旧的项目义则并行留存。

items.en: Twentieth-century policy produced free enterprise, state enterprise and later social enterprise, each fixing one sense in a fixed phrase.
items.cn: 二十世纪的政策产生「自由企业」「国有企业」，后来又出现「社会企业」，每个固定说法都锁定一个义项。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the taking root or look alike; group two holds words for a business or a venture.
note.cn: 第一组是共享「拿取」词根或形近的词；第二组是表示企业或事业的词。

entries.definition: Built on the same French verb, but it names the person who undertakes a venture, not the venture itself.
entries.definitionCN: 同出这个法语动词，但指承担事业的人，不是事业本身。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone full of initiative; it describes a person's drive rather than a firm.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指某人富有主动性；描述人的闯劲，不指企业。

entries.definition: From Latin tenere 'to hold', not from the taking verb, so its similarity to enterprise is only on the surface.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 tenere「握住」，并非出自「拿取」动词，因此与 enterprise 的相似只在表面。

entries.definition: From Latin intrare 'to enter', a different family; it means an opening or the act of coming in.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 intrare「进入」，属另一词族；指入口或进入的动作。

entries.definition: An ordinary word for a firm; it says nothing about boldness or initiative.
entries.definitionCN: 企业的普通说法；不含大胆或进取的意味。

entries.definition: A business, especially a partnership of professionals; more neutral and often smaller in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业，尤指专业人士的合伙机构；更中性，语气上常显得较小。

entries.definition: A new commercial project that involves risk; it stresses the gamble, while enterprise stresses the undertaking.
entries.definitionCN: 指有风险的新商业项目；强调赌注，enterprise 强调承担。

entries.definition: A task or project one has agreed to carry out; closest to the oldest sense of enterprise.

branches.en: UNDERTAKING: a firm and a bold project are both things a group takes on.

branches.en: INITIATIVE: the willingness to take things on is the same word turned into a quality.

branches.en: ACTIVITY AND ORDER: doing business widens into the whole system that permits it.

branches.en: PUBLIC WORKS: dams and state firms are undertakings carried by a public body rather than a private one.
branches.cn: 公共事业：大坝与国有企业是由公共机构而非私人承担的事业。

branches.en: SOCIAL MISSION: what is undertaken becomes a public good instead of a profit.
branches.cn: 社会使命：被承担的东西变成公共利益，而非利润。

senses.title: Someone who starts a venture
senses.definition: a person who sets up a new business, usually committing their own money and effort
senses.definitionCN: 创办新企业的人，通常投入自己的钱与精力
senses.example: The young entrepreneur put her entire savings into a new drying machine and opened a self-service laundry.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻创业者把全部积蓄投进一台新烘干机，开了一家自助洗衣店。
senses.why: The French source means 'one who undertakes', so the word names the person who takes a venture in hand.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为「承担者」，因此这个词指把事业接到手里的人。

senses.title: An organizer of the factors of production
senses.titleCN: 组织生产要素的企业家
senses.definition: in economics, the person who combines capital, labour and materials into a working business
senses.definitionCN: 经济学上把资本、劳动与原料组合成可运转企业的人
senses.example: The textbook defines the entrepreneur as the one who coordinates land, labour and capital.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书把企业家定义为协调土地、劳动与资本的人。
senses.why: Classical economics needed a name for the agent who assembles the other inputs, and borrowed this French word for it.
senses.whyCN: 古典经济学需要为「把其他要素组合起来的人」起个名字，就借用了这个法语词。

senses.title: A self-employed owner-operator
senses.definition: a person who runs their own small business and earns from it rather than from a wage
senses.definitionCN: 经营自己的小企业、靠经营所得而非工资生活的人
senses.example: Many entrepreneurs in the town run one-person workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上许多创业者经营只有一个人的作坊。
senses.why: Owning the venture and working in it are one act for a small operator, so the word covers the self-employed.
senses.whyCN: 对小经营者来说，拥有事业与在其中劳作是同一件事，因此这个词涵盖自雇者。

senses.title: The bearer of business risk
senses.definition: the party who risks their own capital on an uncertain outcome and keeps the residual gain or loss
senses.definitionCN: 把自有资本押在不确定结果上、并承担剩余盈亏的一方
senses.example: The entrepreneur bears the loss if the shop fails.
senses.exampleCN: 如果店铺失败，损失由创业者承担。
senses.why: Undertaking includes taking the downside, so risk bearing became the defining economic mark of the word.
senses.whyCN: 「承担」本来就包含承担坏结果，因此负险成了这个词在经济上的标志。

senses.title: An innovator who breaks old routines
senses.definition: a person who introduces a new product, method or market and displaces established ways of doing things
senses.definitionCN: 引入新产品、新方法或新市场，取代既有做法的人
senses.example: Schumpeter treated the entrepreneur as the force that destroyed old combinations.
senses.exampleCN: 熊彼特把企业家看作摧毁旧组合的力量。
senses.why: Innovation is a form of undertaking: the new combination has to be carried through against existing habits.
senses.whyCN: 创新是承担的一种形态：新的组合必须顶着既有习惯被推行到底。

senses.title: A contractor or promoter of a project
senses.definition: a person who takes on and organizes a specific project, such as a public work or an entertainment
senses.definitionCN: 承接并组织某个具体项目的人，如公共工程或演出
senses.example: The entrepreneur behind the festival booked the whole square.
senses.exampleCN: 操办这个节庆的承办人把整个广场都订下了。
senses.why: The word entered English for the promoter of a musical or theatrical production, and this project sense survives.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初进入英语时指音乐或戏剧演出的承办人，这一项目义保留至今。

senses.title: A repeat founder
senses.definition: a person who starts one venture after another, often selling each before beginning the next
senses.definitionCN: 接连创办事业、常在开始下一个之前卖掉前一个的人
senses.example: The serial entrepreneur had sold three companies by forty.
senses.exampleCN: 这位连续创业者到四十岁时已经卖掉了三家公司。
senses.why: If starting is the core act, repeating it becomes a recognisable type of person.
senses.whyCN: 如果创办是核心动作，反复做这个动作就成为一种可辨认的人。

senses.title: A calculated gambler in business
senses.titleCN: 敢于下注的商界冒险者
senses.definition: a person who commits heavily to an uncertain commercial bet, admired or blamed for boldness
senses.definitionCN: 把大量资源押在不确定的商业赌注上、因大胆而被赞赏或指责的人
senses.example: The entrepreneur staked the factory on a single export contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这位冒险者把整座工厂押在一份出口合同上。
senses.why: Risk bearing pushed to its extreme looks like gambling, and the word takes on that colour in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 把负险推到极端就像赌博，这个词在日常说法里就带上了这层色彩。

intro.en: Entrepreneur is French for 'one who undertakes', from entreprendre 'to take in hand'. English borrowed it in the eighteenth century for a promoter of entertainments, and economics gave it its modern sense in the nineteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: entrepreneur 是法语「承担者」，出自 entreprendre「着手、承担」。英语在十八世纪借入，指演出承办人；经济学在十九世纪赋予它现代含义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Entreprendre 'to undertake' joined a prefix meaning 'between' with prendre 'to take', itself from Latin prehendere 'to grasp'.
items.cn: entreprendre「承担」把意为「之间」的前缀与 prendre「拿取」结合，后者出自拉丁 prehendere「抓住」。

items.en: Entrepreneur named the person who undertakes a task, with no necessary link to trade or profit.
items.cn: entrepreneur 指承担某项任务的人，与买卖或利润没有必然联系。

items.en: English used entrepreneur first for someone who organized public entertainments, especially musical or theatrical productions.
items.cn: 英语最初用 entrepreneur 指组织公共演出的人，尤其是音乐或戏剧制作。

items.en: Nineteenth-century economists, notably Jean-Baptiste Say, made the word mean the agent who combines production and bears the risk.
items.cn: 十九世纪的经济学家，尤其是萨伊，使这个词指组合生产并承担风险的主体。

items.en: Schumpeter shifted the emphasis from mere ownership to innovation, and that reading dominates business writing today.
items.cn: 熊彼特把重点从单纯的所有权转到创新，这一读法如今主导商业写作。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same taking root; group two holds names for people who run or start businesses.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「拿取」词根的词；第二组是经营或创办企业者的称呼。

entries.definition: The undertaking itself, whether a firm or a project; entrepreneur is the person who carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被承担的事业本身，无论企业或项目；entrepreneur 是承担它的人。

entries.definition: An adjective describing the outlook or style of such a person, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述这类人的眼光或风格，不指人本身。

entries.definition: The activity or skill of starting ventures; the noun names the practice, not the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 指创办事业的活动或本领；命名的是实践，不是实践者。

entries.definition: A person who acts like a founder inside an existing company; the prefix marks the setting.
entries.definitionCN: 指在现有公司内部像创办者那样行事的人；前缀标明了场景。

entries.definition: A person who establishes an organization; it records the act of setting up, not the ongoing risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指建立某个组织的人；记录的是创立动作，不是持续承担的风险。

entries.definition: A man engaged in trade; it does not require that he started the firm or bears its risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事买卖的男子；不要求他创办企业或承担其风险。

entries.definition: An owner or manager of large manufacturing enterprises; grander and narrower than entrepreneur.
entries.definitionCN: 指大型制造企业的所有者或管理者；比 entrepreneur 更宏大也更窄。

entries.definition: A promoter of concerts, theatre or opera; it keeps the older English sense of entrepreneur.
entries.definitionCN: 指音乐会、戏剧或歌剧的承办人；保留了 entrepreneur 在英语中较旧的意义。

senses.title: The activity of starting ventures
senses.definition: the activity of identifying an opportunity and building a new business around it
senses.definitionCN: 发现机会并围绕它建立新企业的活动
senses.example: The region's growth was driven by quiet entrepreneurship in small towns.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的增长由小城镇里低调的创业活动推动。
senses.why: The suffix turns the person into a practice: what the undertaker does, repeated across a society, becomes an activity.
senses.whyCN: 后缀把「人」变成「实践」：承担者所做的事，在一个社会里反复发生，就成了活动。

senses.title: The spirit of initiative and risk
senses.titleCN: 创业精神；敢闯敢试的态度
senses.definition: the attitude that welcomes initiative, experiment and the risk of failure
senses.definitionCN: 欢迎主动、试验并接受失败风险的态度
senses.example: The prize honours entrepreneurship as much as profit.
senses.exampleCN: 这个奖项看重创业精神，不亚于看重利润。
senses.why: A practice also becomes a disposition, so the word names the willingness to undertake things at all.
senses.whyCN: 实践也会成为一种性情，因此这个词也指「愿意承担事情」的意愿。

senses.title: The skill of building a business
senses.titleCN: 创业本领；经营新事业的能力
senses.definition: the practical ability to spot a market, raise resources and keep a new firm going
senses.definitionCN: 发现市场、筹集资源并让新企业存活的实际能力
senses.example: She learned entrepreneurship by running the stall for two summers.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠两个夏天守摊学会了创业本领。
senses.why: What begins as an activity is also something one can be good at, so the word shifts from doing to skill.
senses.whyCN: 开始时指活动，也可以指擅长的本事，因此这个词从「做」转向「能力」。

senses.title: The academic field that studies it
senses.titleCN: 创业学；创业课程与研究领域
senses.definition: the university subject that studies how ventures are created, financed and grown
senses.definitionCN: 研究事业如何被创造、筹资与成长的高校学科
senses.example: At this vocational school, the entrepreneurship course runs inside a real shop on the street.
senses.exampleCN: 这所职业学校把创业课直接开在街边的真实铺面里。
senses.why: Once a practice is studied and taught, its name attaches to the department and the course.
senses.whyCN: 一种实践被研究与教授之后，它的名称就挂到系所与课程上。

senses.title: The surrounding ecosystem
senses.titleCN: 创业生态；支撑创业的环境
senses.definition: the network of finance, mentors, rules and customers that lets ventures start and scale
senses.definitionCN: 让事业得以启动与扩张的资金、导师、规则与客户网络
senses.example: Cheap loans and open data built a lively entrepreneurship in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价贷款与开放数据在这座城市培育出活跃的创业生态。
senses.why: Individual ventures depend on shared conditions, so the practice is also named as a surrounding system.
senses.whyCN: 单个事业依赖共同条件，因此这种实践也被命名为一个环绕的系统。

senses.title: Venturing for a social goal
senses.titleCN: 社会创业；以社会目标为导向的创业
senses.definition: the practice of building enterprises whose main aim is social or environmental benefit
senses.definitionCN: 建立以社会或环境效益为主要目标的企业实践
senses.example: Social entrepreneurship has brought cheap spectacles to rural clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 社会创业让乡村诊所有了便宜的眼镜。
senses.why: The undertaking can serve a public purpose, so a modifier marks the goal rather than the method.
senses.whyCN: 承担之事可以服务公共目的，于是用修饰语标出目标而非方法。

senses.title: Venturing inside an existing firm
senses.titleCN: 机构内创业；企业内部创新
senses.definition: the practice of starting new projects with an owner's freedom inside an established organization
senses.definitionCN: 在既有组织内部以创办者的自由启动新项目的实践
senses.example: The group encourages intrapreneurship among its engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 该集团鼓励工程师进行机构内创业。
senses.why: The undertaking does not need a new company, so a variant word marks the same act performed inside one.
senses.whyCN: 承担事业并不需要新公司，因此一个变体词标记在同一家公司内部完成的同一动作。

senses.title: The measured rate of new ventures
senses.titleCN: 创业率；创业活动的总量指标
senses.definition: the statistical level of new business formation in an economy or region
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体或地区新企业形成的统计水平
senses.example: Surveys now track entrepreneurship as a share of the workforce.
senses.exampleCN: 调查如今把创业率作为劳动人口的一个比重来追踪。
senses.why: Governments need to count what they wish to encourage, so the practice becomes a statistic.
senses.whyCN: 政府需要数清自己想要鼓励的东西，于是这种实践变成一个统计量。

intro.en: Entrepreneurship is entrepreneur plus the English suffix -ship, from Old English -scipe 'state, condition'. The word is a modern formation, spread by economics and business schools. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: entrepreneurship 是 entrepreneur 加英语后缀 -ship 构成，后者源自古英语 -scipe「状态、情形」。这个词是近代构词，由经济学与商学院推广开来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Entrepreneur, 'one who undertakes', came from entreprendre 'to take in hand', built on Latin prehendere 'to grasp'.
items.cn: entrepreneur「承担者」来自 entreprendre「着手、承担」，由拉丁 prehendere「抓住」构成。

items.en: The suffix -scipe named a state or condition and survives in friendship, hardship and leadership; it turns a person into a practice or role.
items.cn: 后缀 -scipe 表示状态或情形，保留在 friendship、hardship 与 leadership 中；它把「人」变成实践或身份。

items.en: English joined the two elements to name the activity of the entrepreneur, at first in economic writing about production and risk.
items.cn: 英语把两个成分合起来，命名企业家所从事的活动，最初见于关于生产与风险的经济论述。

items.en: Twentieth-century business schools made the word a subject with courses, journals and textbooks.
items.cn: 二十世纪的商学院使这个词成为一门有课程、期刊与教科书的学科。

items.en: Governments began to measure and promote entrepreneurship, and the word acquired a statistical sense.
items.cn: 各国政府开始测量并促进创业，这个词于是取得统计义。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same word; group two holds wider words for the activity of building something new.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的各种形式；第二组是表示「开创新事物」这一活动的更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: The undertaker himself or herself; the practice noun adds the activity around that person.
entries.definitionCN: 指承担者本人；这个实践名词加上的是围绕那个人的活动。

entries.definition: An adjective for the outlook or style, not the field of study or the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指那种眼光或风格，不指学科领域或活动。

entries.definition: Simply more than one founder; it counts people rather than practice.
entries.definitionCN: 只是不止一位创办者；数的是人，不是实践。

entries.definition: The same practice carried out inside an existing organization, marked by a prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 同一实践在既有组织内部进行，由前缀标出场景。

entries.definition: A firm, a project or the general drive to undertake things; broader and less technical than entrepreneurship.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业、项目或承担事情的劲头；比 entrepreneurship 更宽、更不技术化。

entries.definition: A single commercial project with risk attached; entrepreneurship is the whole practice of making such projects.
entries.definitionCN: 指单独一个有风险的商业项目；entrepreneurship 是制造这类项目的整体实践。

entries.definition: The readiness to act first without being told; it is a personal quality, not a field of activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指无需吩咐就先行行动的意愿；是个人品质，不是活动领域。

entries.definition: The introduction of something new; it can happen inside a firm and need not involve founding one.
entries.definitionCN: 指引入新事物；可在企业内部发生，不必创办企业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Entrepreneur plus the state suffix: the condition of being one who undertakes.
normal.cn: entrepreneur 加状态后缀：身为承担者的状态。

normal.en: The family runs entrepreneur, entrepreneurial, entrepreneurship and intrapreneurship.
normal.cn: 同族词有 entrepreneur、entrepreneurial、entrepreneurship 与 intrapreneurship。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: a course in entrepreneurship, social entrepreneurship, a culture of entrepreneurship.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各义项：创业课程、社会创业、创业文化。

normal.en: The suffix also builds friendship and leadership, all states or roles.
normal.cn: 同一后缀还构成 friendship 与 leadership，都表示状态或身份。

normal.en: Economics measures it as a rate, schools teach it as a subject.
normal.cn: 经济学把它当比率来测量，学校把它当学科来教授。

abstract.cn: 想象一间空铺面，招牌还没刷，货架已经摆满。

abstract.cn: 想象一间教室，课桌换成了柜台与钱箱。

examples.cn: 该基金会为青少年举办创业工作坊。

examples.en: Social entrepreneurship attracts graduates who want measurable impact.
examples.cn: 社会创业吸引希望看到可衡量影响的毕业生。

examples.en: Low barriers to registration are linked to higher entrepreneurship.
examples.cn: 较低的注册门槛与更高的创业率相关。

root: 英语构词：entrepreneur（法语「承担者」，出自拉丁 prehendere「抓住」）+ 古英语后缀 -ship（状态、身份）；指创办与经营新事业的活动、精神与学科。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one practice: the activity, the spirit, the skill, the academic field, the ecosystem, the social variant, the in-house variant, and the statistical rate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种实践：活动、精神、本领、学科、生态、社会版本、机构内版本，以及统计上的比率。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty shop being fitted with shelves before the sign is painted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间空铺面正在装货架，招牌还没刷。

branches.en: DOING AND BEING ABLE: the activity and the skill are the same practice seen from outside and inside.
branches.cn: 做与能做：活动与本领，是同一实践从外部和内部看到的两种样子。

branches.en: DISPOSITION: the willingness to undertake becomes a character trait.
branches.cn: 性情：愿意承担事情的意愿成为一种性格。

branches.en: TAUGHT AND SUPPORTED: a subject in a classroom and an ecosystem of finance and mentors both surround the practice.
branches.cn: 被教授与被支撑：课堂里的学科与资金导师构成的生态，都环绕着这种实践。

branches.en: TWO DIRECTIONS: the same undertaking can aim at a public good or happen inside an existing firm.
branches.cn: 两个方向：同样的承担可以指向公共利益，也可以发生在既有企业内部。

branches.en: COUNTED: what is encouraged must be measured, so the practice becomes a rate.
branches.cn: 被计数：被鼓励的东西必须被测量，于是这种实践变成一个比率。

intro.en: Entrepreneurship joins a French agent noun to an Old English state suffix, so it mixes two language layers.
intro.cn: entrepreneurship 把法语施事名词与古英语状态后缀接在一起，因此混合了两个语言层。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is prehendere 'to grasp'; the suffix layer is Old English -scipe, seen in friendship and leadership.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 prehendere「抓住」；后缀层是古英语 -scipe，见于 friendship 与 leadership。

items.example: The entrepreneur opened a laundry.

items.example: The team had an entrepreneurial style.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队有创业风格。

items.example: The school teaches entrepreneurship.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校教授创业。

items.example: The suffix also builds leadership.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀还构成 leadership。

items.example: The lab supports intrapreneurship.

items.meaningCN: 以社会目标为导向的创业
items.example: Social entrepreneurship funded the clinic.
items.exampleCN: 社会创业为诊所提供了资金。

definition_zh: 创业的；有创业精神的；企业家式的；敢冒风险开创新事的
definition_en: relating to someone who starts businesses, or showing the initiative and risk-taking of such a person
core_image: 一间公司里，几个人把旧流程撕下，换上自己画的新流程图

sceneCN: 她把公司里最敢试错的一组人单独拉出来做新项目；句中的 entrepreneurial 指「具有主动开创与试错精神的」（第 2 个义项：具有创业精神的）。图中可辨识物件：新流程图、白板、旧流程纸、项目挂牌。

pos.zh: 创业的；有创业精神的；企业家式的；敢冒风险的

senses.title: Relating to people who start businesses
senses.titleCN: 创业的；与创办企业有关的
senses.definition: connected with entrepreneurs or with the founding of new businesses
senses.definitionCN: 与创业者或与新企业创办有关的
senses.example: The city runs an entrepreneurial grant for first-time founders.
senses.exampleCN: 该市为首次创办者提供一笔创业补助。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the person to a noun, saying that the thing belongs to the world of founders.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把那个人挂到名词上，说明所指数事物属于创办者的世界。

senses.title: Showing initiative and willingness to try
senses.titleCN: 具有主动开创与试错精神的
senses.definition: showing the drive to begin new things and to try methods that may fail
senses.definitionCN: 表现出启动新事、并尝试可能失败的方法的劲头
senses.example: She pulled the most entrepreneurial team in the company out to run a new project.
senses.exampleCN: 她把公司里最敢试错的一组人单独拉出来做新项目。
senses.why: The person noun carries the drive to undertake, and the adjective transfers that drive onto a team or a attitude.
senses.whyCN: 指人的名词本身带着「承担」的劲头，形容词把这种劲头转移到团队或态度上。

senses.title: Businesslike in a creative, deal-making way
senses.titleCN: 企业家式的；善于经营与撮合的
senses.definition: acting with the resourcefulness and deal-making skill associated with business owners
senses.definitionCN: 以企业主那种善找资源、善撮合交易的方式行事
senses.example: He took an entrepreneurial approach to the empty warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 他以企业家式的办法处理那间空仓库。
senses.why: Owners must find money, partners and customers at once, and the adjective names that combined knack.
senses.whyCN: 企业主必须同时找钱、找伙伴、找客户，这个形容词命名的是这种综合本事。

senses.title: Ready to accept financial risk
senses.definition: willing to commit money or resources to an uncertain outcome
senses.definitionCN: 愿意把钱或资源押在不确定结果上的
senses.example: Their entrepreneurial bet on the new line almost failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在新产线上的冒险押注几乎失败。
senses.why: Risk bearing is the economic core of the founder, and the adjective marks that readiness.
senses.whyCN: 承担风险是创办者在经济上的核心，这个形容词标记的就是这种准备。

senses.title: Enterprising and full of drive
senses.definition: energetic and eager to seize opportunities rather than wait for instruction
senses.definitionCN: 有精力、急于抓住机会，而不是等别人吩咐
senses.example: The most entrepreneurial students ran the market stall themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 最有闯劲的学生自己操办了集市摊位。
senses.why: If the practice is undertaking, the adjective also describes the temperament that undertakes readily.
senses.whyCN: 如果这种实践是「承担」，这个形容词也描述那种乐于承担的性格。

senses.title: Given freedom to act like an owner
senses.titleCN: 被赋予自主开拓空间的（团队、岗位）
senses.definition: describing a role or unit that is allowed to experiment and decide without close supervision
senses.definitionCN: 描述被允许试验、无须紧密监督即可决定的岗位或单元
senses.example: The firm created an entrepreneurial unit with its own budget.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司设立了一个拥有独立预算的自主开拓单元。
senses.why: Firms borrow the founder's freedom for selected teams, and the adjective marks that granted autonomy.
senses.whyCN: 公司把创办者的自由借给特定团队，这个形容词标记的是被授予的自主。

senses.title: Describing an economy or culture of founders
senses.titleCN: 创业型的（经济、文化、地区）
senses.definition: used of an economy, region or culture in which starting businesses is common and valued
senses.definitionCN: 用于创办企业普遍且受重视的经济、地区或文化
senses.example: The province developed an entrepreneurial economy after the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 改革之后，该省发展出一种创业型经济。
senses.why: Many founders acting at once create a climate, and the adjective can describe that climate.
senses.whyCN: 许多创办者同时行动会形成一种气候，这个形容词也用来描述那种气候。

senses.title: Quick to spot an opportunity
senses.definition: skilled at noticing an unmet need and turning it into a commercial opening
senses.definitionCN: 擅长察觉未被满足的需求并把它变成商业机会
senses.example: Her entrepreneurial eye noticed the queue nobody was serving.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种善于发现机会的眼光注意到没人服务的队伍。
senses.why: Opportunity is the raw material a founder works with, so the adjective also names the ability to see it.
senses.whyCN: 机会是创办者的原料，因此这个形容词也命名看见它的能力。

intro.en: Entrepreneurial is entrepreneur plus the adjectival suffix -ial, from Latin -alis. English built the adjective in the nineteenth century alongside the economic sense of the noun. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: entrepreneurial 是 entrepreneur 加上形容词后缀 -ial 构成，后者出自拉丁 -alis。英语在十九世纪随名词的经济义一同造出这个形容词。年代均为约数。

items.en: The base verb meant 'to take in hand, undertake', built on Latin prehendere 'to grasp'.
items.cn: 基础动词意为「着手、承担」，由拉丁 prehendere「抓住」构成。

items.en: The person noun named one who undertakes a venture, and English borrowed it in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 指人的名词指承担事业者，英语在十八世纪借入。

items.en: The suffix -alis formed adjectives of relation in Latin and became -al and -ial in English, as in financial and commercial.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 在拉丁语中构成关系形容词，在英语中变成 -al 与 -ial，如 financial 与 commercial。

items.en: Economists needed an adjective for the new noun, and entrepreneurial appeared to describe ventures, risk and behaviour.
items.cn: 经济学家需要为这个新名词配一个形容词，entrepreneurial 遂出现，描述事业、风险与行为。

items.en: Twentieth-century management writing extended it to teams, units and whole cultures, widening its range.
items.cn: 二十世纪的管理写作把它扩展到团队、单元与整体文化，拓宽了它的范围。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same word; group two holds adjectives for similar temperaments.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的各种形式；第二组是描述相近性情的形容词。

entries.definition: The founder himself or herself; the adjective describes the quality rather than the person.
entries.definitionCN: 指创办者本人；形容词描述的是性质，不是人。

entries.definition: The activity or field; the adjective cannot replace it as the subject of a course.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动或领域；形容词不能替代它作课程的科目名。

entries.definition: An older adjective meaning full of initiative, without the economic and risk-bearing weight of entrepreneurial.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的形容词，指富有主动性，没有 entrepreneurial 的经济与负险分量。

entries.definition: The same adjective applied to founder-like behaviour inside an existing organization.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词，用于既有组织内部类似创办者的行为。

entries.definition: Introducing new ideas or methods; it stresses novelty, not ownership or financial risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指引入新想法或方法；强调新颖，不强调所有权或财务风险。

entries.definition: Acting in advance rather than reacting; it describes timing, while entrepreneurial describes outlook.
entries.definitionCN: 指提前行动而非被动反应；描述时机，entrepreneurial 描述眼光。

entries.definition: Willing to take risks, often physical ones; narrower and more hazardous in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指愿意冒险，常指身体上的风险；范围更窄，语气更危险。

entries.definition: Eager for success and achievement; it may lack the commercial and experimental colour.
entries.definitionCN: 指渴望成功与成就；可能缺少商业与试验的色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Entrepreneur plus the relating suffix: belonging to the founder's world.
normal.cn: entrepreneur 加关系后缀：属于创办者的世界。

normal.en: The family runs entrepreneur, entrepreneurial, entrepreneurship and intrapreneurial.
normal.cn: 同族词有 entrepreneur、entrepreneurial、entrepreneurship 与 intrapreneurial。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: an entrepreneurial culture, entrepreneurial skills, entrepreneurial spirit.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各义项：创业文化、创业技能、创业精神。

normal.en: The Latin relating suffix also builds financial and commercial.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁关系后缀还构成 financial 与 commercial。

normal.en: Management writing applies it to units and budgets, not only to people.
normal.cn: 管理写作把它用到单元与预算上，不只用于人。

abstract.en: Picture an old flow chart torn off a wall and a hand-drawn one pinned in its place.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一张旧流程图被撕下，一张手绘的钉在原来的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a locked room with one key left on the table for whoever dares to use it.
abstract.cn: 想象一间上锁的房间，桌上留着一把钥匙，谁敢用就归谁。

abstract.cn: 想象一条没人招呼的队伍，旁边已有人支起了摊子。

examples.cn: 该项目向有创业精神的女性提供小额贷款。

examples.cn: 一位有闯劲的经理在一家分行试行了新服务。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: belonging to founders, showing initiative, businesslike resourcefulness, accepting risk, enterprising, granted autonomy, describing a regional culture, and spotting opportunity.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个形容词：属于创办者、显出主动性、善于撮合资源、接受风险、有闯劲、被赋予自主、描述地区文化，以及善于发现机会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old flow chart torn down and a hand-drawn one pinned up.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧流程图被撕下，手绘的新图钉了上去。

branches.en: BELONGING TO FOUNDERS: one firm's adjective and a whole region's climate describe the same world at different scales.
branches.cn: 属于创办者：一家企业的形容词与整个地区的气候，是同一世界的两种尺度。

branches.en: DRIVE: willingness to begin and readiness to seize an occasion are one temperament.
branches.cn: 闯劲：愿意开始与急于抓住时机，是同一种性情。

branches.en: RESOURCEFUL: finding money, partners and customers at once is the founder's knack.
branches.cn: 善找资源：同时找钱、找伙伴与找客户，是创办者的本事。

branches.en: RISK: committing money to an uncertain outcome is the economic core.
branches.cn: 风险：把钱押在不确定结果上，是经济上的核心。

branches.en: GRANTED FREEDOM: a team allowed to act like an owner is expected to notice what others miss.
branches.cn: 被授予自由：被允许像业主那样行动的团队，被期待看见别人漏掉的东西。

intro.en: Entrepreneurial is a French agent noun plus a Latin relating suffix, a very common English pattern.
intro.cn: entrepreneurial 是法语施事名词加拉丁关系后缀，是英语中极常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: Latin prehendere supplies the root; Latin -alis supplies the suffix seen in financial, commercial and manual.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prehendere 提供词根；拉丁 -alis 提供后缀，见于 financial、commercial 与 manual。

items.example: The team had an entrepreneurial style.

items.example: The fund was used entrepreneurially.
items.exampleCN: 这笔资金被以创业的方式使用。

items.example: The school teaches entrepreneurship.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校教授创业。

items.meaningCN: 在企业内部像创办者那样的
items.example: The unit was given an intrapreneurial budget.

definition_zh: 公司；法人；大型企业；法人团体；（英国旧用法）市政当局
definition_en: a large company or a legally recognized group of people treated as a single body
core_image: 围墙里面一整片园区，办公楼、食堂与厂房各自运转，门口只有一块法人名牌
scene: 那家公司在河边建起整片园区，围墙内自成一城。The corporation built a whole campus by the river, a city of its own behind the fence.
sceneCN: 那家公司在河边建起整片园区，围墙内自成一城；句中的 corporation 指「被当作单一法律主体的大型企业」（第 1 个义项：法人企业、公司）。图中可辨识物件：园区围墙、办公楼、厂房屋顶、法人名牌。

pos.zh: 公司；法人；大型企业；法人团体
市政当局；市自治体

senses.title: A company recognized as one legal person
senses.titleCN: 被承认为单一法律主体的公司
senses.definition: a business organization that the law treats as a single person separate from its owners
senses.definitionCN: 法律视作与其所有者分离的单一「人」的商业组织
senses.example: The corporation built a whole campus by the river, a city of its own behind the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 那家公司在河边建起整片园区，围墙内自成一城。
senses.why: Corporation comes from the Latin word for a body, and the law's image is exactly that: many people fused into one body.
senses.whyCN: corporation 出自拉丁语「身体」一词，法律的意象正是如此：许多人合成一个身体。

senses.title: A very large business group
senses.definition: a large company, especially one with many divisions, employees and countries of operation
senses.definitionCN: 规模庞大的公司，尤指拥有众多部门、员工与跨国业务者
senses.example: The corporation employs more people than the town where it began.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司雇的人比它起家的那座镇子人口还多。
senses.why: Because the legal form was adopted by big ventures, the word acquired a tone of size and distance.
senses.whyCN: 由于大企业多采用这种法律形式，这个词便带上了规模与距离感。

senses.title: Any legally created body
senses.definition: a group of people or an office given legal personality, such as a city, a university or a charity
senses.definitionCN: 被赋予法律人格的一群人或不职位，如城市、大学或慈善机构
senses.example: The university is a corporation with its own seal and statutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学是一个拥有自己的印章与章程的法人。
senses.why: The body image does not require trade, so the word covers any group the law makes into one person.
senses.whyCN: 「身体」的意象并不要求买卖，因此这个词涵盖法律合成为一个人的任何团体。

senses.title: A company with limited liability for shareholders
senses.titleCN: 股东有限责任的股份公司
senses.definition: a company whose shareholders are liable only up to what they invested, not for the company's debts
senses.definitionCN: 股东只以其出资额为限负责、不为公司债务负责的公司
senses.example: Investors preferred the corporation because their own homes were protected.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者偏爱这种股份公司，因为自己的住房受到保护。
senses.why: Separating the body from its members is what makes limited liability possible, so the form and the protection share one name.
senses.whyCN: 把「身体」与成员分开，才使有限责任成为可能，因此形式与保护共用一个名称。

senses.title: A city authority, in older British usage
senses.titleCN: （英国旧用法）市政当局；市自治体
senses.definition: the governing body of a town or city, historically chartered as a legal corporation
senses.definitionCN: 城镇的治理机构，历史上以法人特许状设立
senses.example: The old corporation still maintains the bridge and the market cross.
senses.exampleCN: 旧的市政当局仍在维护那座桥与市场十字架。
senses.why: A chartered town was literally a body corporate, so the same word served for municipal government before it served for business.
senses.whyCN: 获特许的城镇本身就是法人团体，因此这个词先用于市政，后用于商业。

senses.title: A public body set up by statute
senses.titleCN: 依法设立的公共法人；公营公司
senses.definition: a public authority or state-owned body created by law to run a service
senses.definitionCN: 依法设立、负责某项公共服务的公营机构或国有企业
senses.example: The transport corporation answers to the ministry, not to shareholders.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公共法人向部委负责，而不向股东负责。
senses.why: Public services also need a legal body, so the word splits into private and public branches.
senses.whyCN: 公共服务也需要一个法律身体，于是这个词分出私营与公营两支。

senses.title: Used before a noun: of corporate business
senses.titleCN: 作定语：企业层面的、公司的
senses.definition: placed before nouns such as tax, law or headquarters to mark the business-entity level
senses.definitionCN: 置于税、法、总部等名词前，标记企业实体这一层面
senses.example: Corporation tax is charged on profits, not on the owners' incomes.
senses.exampleCN: 企业税按利润征收，不按所有者个人收入征收。
senses.why: Once the form became standard, it served as a classifier distinguishing company-level matters from personal ones.
senses.whyCN: 这种形式普及之后，它就成了分类词，把企业层面的事务与个人事务区分开。

senses.title: A guild or professional body, historically
senses.definition: a chartered association of craftsmen or professionals with collective rights
senses.definitionCN: 拥有集体权利、经特许设立的手工业者或专业人士团体
senses.example: The guild was incorporated as a corporation in the fifteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行会在十五世纪被设为法人团体。
senses.why: Medieval guilds were the first bodies the law treated as single persons, long before trading companies.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的行会是最早被法律当作单一人格的团体，远早于贸易公司。

intro.en: Corporation comes from Latin corporatio 'a body', from corporare 'to form into a body', from corpus 'body'. Medieval law used it for guilds and towns before it named trading companies. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: corporation 来自拉丁 corporatio「身体」，出自 corporare「使成为身体」，再溯至 corpus「身体」。中世纪法律先用它指行会与城镇，后来才指贸易公司。年代均为约数。

items.en: Corpus meant 'body', and Roman law already spoke of a group as one body, a universitas or corpus.
items.cn: corpus 意为「身体」，罗马法已把一群人称作一个身体，即团体或身体。

items.en: Medieval Latin corporatio named the act of forming a body and the body so formed, applied to guilds, monasteries and towns.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 corporatio 指「形成身体」的行为及所形成之体，用于行会、修道院与城镇。

items.en: English borrowed the word for chartered bodies, and a town or a guild could hold property and sue as one person.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词指经特许的团体，城镇或行会可以作为一个「人」持有财产、提起诉讼。

items.en: From the sixteenth century chartered trading companies took the form, and corporation drifted towards commercial meaning.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，经特许的贸易公司采用这一形式，corporation 逐渐转向商业含义。

items.en: In the nineteenth century general incorporation laws made the corporate form ordinary for business, and the modern sense settled.
items.cn: 十九世纪的一般法人法使这种形式成为企业的常规选择，现代义由此定型。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same body root; group two holds other names for a business entity.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「身体」词根的词；第二组是商业实体的其他称呼。

entries.definition: Relating to a corporation; it describes the level or style, not the entity.
entries.definitionCN: 与公司有关的形容词；描述层面或风格，不指实体。

entries.definition: To form a legal corporation or to bring something into a whole; the action, not the body.
entries.definitionCN: 指组成法人，或把某物并入整体；是动作，不是那个身体。

entries.definition: A system in which interest groups negotiate with the state; it looks similar but names politics, not a firm.
entries.definitionCN: 指利益团体与国家协商的制度；形近，但命名的是政治制度，不是企业。

entries.definition: From the same Latin word for body, but it means a dead body; the shared root is not a shared meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁「身体」一词，但指尸体；词根相同不代表意义相同。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for a business; it does not imply the legal person or the large scale.
entries.definitionCN: 企业的日常说法；不含法律人格或大规模的意思。

entries.definition: A business, often a partnership of professionals; usually smaller and less formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业，常为专业人士合伙；语气上通常较小、较不正式。

entries.definition: A group of companies in unrelated industries; a corporation may be one, but need not be.
entries.definitionCN: 指跨不相关行业的公司群；公司可能是其中一种，但不必是。

entries.definition: A business or a bold project; it stresses activity and initiative rather than legal structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业或大胆项目；强调活动与主动，不强调法律结构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Latin for body: many people fused into one legal body.
normal.cn: 拉丁语意为「身体」：许多人合成一个法律身体。

normal.en: The family runs corporation, corporate, incorporate, incorporation and corporatism.
normal.cn: 同族词有 corporation、corporate、incorporate、incorporation 与 corporatism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: a multinational corporation, corporation tax, a public corporation.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各义项：跨国公司、企业税、公营公司。

normal.en: The same root gives corpse and corporeal, all about bodies.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 corpse 与 corporeal，都与身体有关。

normal.en: Historically it meant a town or a guild before it meant a trading company.
normal.cn: 在指贸易公司之前，它先指城镇或行会。

abstract.en: Picture a fence around a whole district with one name plate at the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一整片城区被围墙圈住，大门上只有一块名牌。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred signatures on one document that the law reads as a single hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件上有一百个签名，法律却把它读作一只手。

abstract.en: Picture a body whose limbs move on their own but share one pulse.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身体，四肢各自活动，却共享一个脉搏。

examples.en: The corporation reported record profits but cut its workforce.
examples.cn: 这家公司报告了创纪录的利润，却裁减了员工。

examples.en: A corporation can own property and be sued in its own name.
examples.cn: 公司可以以自己的名义拥有财产并被起诉。

examples.en: The city corporation manages the harbour under an old charter.
examples.cn: 该市市政当局依据旧特许状管理港口。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one legal body: the incorporated company, the large group, any chartered body, the limited-liability form, the municipal authority, the public corporation, the attributive label, and the medieval guild.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个「法律身体」：法人公司、大型集团、任何依法成立的团体、有限责任形式、市政当局、公营法人、定语标签，以及中世纪行会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walled campus that the law treats as one person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片被围墙圈住的园区，法律把它当作一个人。

branches.en: BODY AT TWO SIZES: the legal person and the giant group are the same structure at different scales.
branches.cn: 两种尺度的身体：法律人格与巨型集团，是同一结构的不同规模。

branches.en: ANY CHARTERED BODY: a university, a town and a guild are all groups the law makes into one person.
branches.cn: 任何特许团体：大学、城镇与行会，都是法律合成为一个人的群体。

branches.en: SEPARATE POCKET: because the body is distinct from its members, their own property is shielded.
branches.cn: 分开的口袋：因为身体与成员有别，成员自己的财产才受到保护。

branches.en: PUBLIC BRANCH: municipal and statutory bodies show the form does not require private owners.
branches.cn: 公营分支：市政与法定机构说明这种形式并不需要私人所有者。

branches.en: CLASSIFIER: the name turns into a marker for company-level tax, law and offices.
branches.cn: 分类词：这个名称变成企业层面税务、法律与机构的标记。

intro.en: Corporation is a Latin body word with an action suffix; the same root builds most of the vocabulary of corporate law.
intro.cn: corporation 是拉丁「身体」一词加动作后缀；同一词根构成公司法的大部分词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin corpus gives corpse, corporeal and incorporate; corporare gives corporation and incorporation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 corpus 给出 corpse、corporeal 与 incorporate；corporare 给出 corporation 与 incorporation。

items.exampleCN: 罗马法把一群人称作一个身体。

items.example: The verb names the act of fusing members.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名把成员合成的动作。

items.meaningCN: 形成身体（的行为或结果）
items.example: The medieval term named guilds and towns.

items.example: The corporation built the campus.

items.example: Corporate tax applies to profits.
items.exampleCN: 企业税适用于利润。

items.example: The partners incorporated in spring.
items.exampleCN: 合伙人春天注册成了法人。

items.meaning: the act of forming a corporation
items.example: Incorporation limited their personal liability.

items.example: The right applies to corporeal property.

latinEntries.meaning: a forming into a body; a body so formed
latinEntries.meaningCN: 形成身体；由此形成的团体

definition_zh: 公司；陪伴；客人；一群人；（军事）连；剧团
definition_en: a business organization, the state of being with other people, guests, or a group of people who share an activity
core_image: 一间小铺子里，几个人围着同一张工作台，各自手上都有活
scene: 这家只有六个人的小公司靠修表为生。The tiny company of six people survives by repairing watches.
sceneCN: 这家只有六个人的小公司靠修表为生；句中的 company 指「以经营为业的商业组织」（第 1 个义项：公司、商号）。图中可辨识物件：放大镜、钟表零件、工作台、招牌。

pos.zh: 公司；陪伴；客人；一群人；连队；剧团

senses.title: A business organization
senses.definition: a business that sells goods or services, whether small or large
senses.definitionCN: 出售货物或服务的企业，无论大小
senses.example: The tiny company of six people survives by repairing watches.
senses.exampleCN: 这家只有六个人的小公司靠修表为生。
senses.why: The word began as 'those who share bread', and a firm is a group of people sharing a livelihood; the trading sense grew from that group.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「同吃面包的人」，而企业正是一群共享生计的人；商业义就从这个群体生长出来。

senses.title: The state of having someone with you
senses.definition: the presence of another person, especially one whose presence is comforting
senses.definitionCN: 另一个人在身旁，尤指其存在令人安心
senses.example: She stayed for the company as much as for the meal.
senses.exampleCN: 她留下来，一半是为了有人作伴，一半是为了吃饭。
senses.why: Sharing bread is also sharing time, so the oldest sense of the word is simply being together.
senses.whyCN: 同吃面包也是共度时间，因此这个词最古老的意思就是「在一起」。

senses.title: Guests or visitors
senses.definition: people who are visiting, especially when their visit is expected or welcome
senses.definitionCN: 来访的人，尤指其到访在预期之中或受欢迎
senses.example: We are expecting company on Sunday, so the table will be full.
senses.exampleCN: 周日我们有客人来，桌子会坐满。
senses.why: If company is people being together, then visitors are the company one has in the house.
senses.whyCN: 如果 company 是一群人在一起，那么来客就是家里「有的那批人」。

senses.title: A group bound by a shared activity
senses.titleCN: 一群共同从事某项活动的人
senses.definition: a group of people who do something together, such as actors, singers or travellers
senses.definitionCN: 一起做某件事的一群人，如演员、歌手或旅人
senses.example: A company of actors arrived with three trunks and no scenery.
senses.exampleCN: 一队演员带着三只箱子来了，没有布景。
senses.why: A body of people acting together is the literal middle of the word's history, between companionship and business.
senses.whyCN: 共同行动的一群人，正是这个词历史中段的字面意思，介于「作伴」与「经商」之间。

senses.title: A military unit
senses.definition: a unit of soldiers, usually part of a battalion and commanded by a captain
senses.definitionCN: 士兵的编制单位，通常隶属某一营，由上尉指挥
senses.example: The company held the bridge until dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个连守住了桥，一直到天亮。
senses.why: Armed men organized together were a company before merchants were, and the military sense kept the older group meaning.
senses.whyCN: 武装起来共同行动的一群人在商人之前就被称作 company，军事义保留了较旧的「群体」含义。

senses.title: Association with someone
senses.definition: the act of spending time with a person or group, often with a moral shade in the phrase
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某群体共度时间，在固定说法里常带道德意味
senses.example: He kept company with sailors and learned their songs.
senses.exampleCN: 他与水手们结伴，学会了他们的歌。
senses.why: Being together repeatedly is a relation, so company also means the association itself, not just the people.
senses.whyCN: 反复在一起就成了一种关系，因此 company 也指交往本身，而不只是那些人。

senses.title: A theatre or opera troupe
senses.definition: a permanent group of performers working under one management
senses.definitionCN: 在同一管理下演出的常设表演团体
senses.example: The opera company tours the provinces every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这家歌剧团每年秋天到各省巡演。
senses.why: Performers are a company in the old sense of a body of people, and the theatre kept the word after commerce took it over.
senses.whyCN: 演员是按「一群人」旧义所说的 company，商业占用这个词之后，剧场仍保留了它。

senses.title: A chartered trading society
senses.titleCN: （历史）特许贸易商团；合伙商号
senses.definition: a chartered society of merchants trading collectively under a monopoly, such as the old East India companies
senses.definitionCN: 经特许、以垄断方式集体贸易的商人团体，如旧时的东印度公司
senses.example: The merchants formed a company and petitioned for a charter.
senses.exampleCN: 商人们组成一个商团，申请特许状。
senses.why: When merchants pooled capital under a charter, the group name became the business name, and modern companies inherit it.
senses.whyCN: 当商人在特许状下合资经营，群体名称就成了企业名称，现代公司由此继承。

intro.en: Company comes from Old French compaignie 'fellowship', from Late Latin companio 'one who shares bread', built on com- 'with' and panis 'bread'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: company 来自古法语 compaignie「同伴关系」，再溯至晚期拉丁 companio「同吃面包的人」，由 com-「共同」与 panis「面包」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Panis meant 'bread', and the Late Latin noun companio named a person who eats bread with another.
items.cn: panis 意为「面包」，晚期拉丁名词 companio 指与另一个人同吃面包的人。

items.en: Old French turned the noun into compaignie, 'fellowship, society', and the word entered English with the sense of being together.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词变成 compaignie「同伴关系、团体」，进入英语时意为「在一起」。

items.en: Medieval usage applied it to a body of soldiers under one captain, fixing the group sense.
items.cn: 中世纪的用法把它用于由一名上尉统领的一队士兵，固定了「群体」义。

items.en: From the sixteenth century chartered merchant societies were called companies, and the commercial sense became dominant.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，经特许的商人团体被称为 company，商业义逐渐占主导。

items.en: Industrial law made company the standard word for an incorporated business, while the older senses survived in fixed phrases.
items.cn: 工业时代的法律使 company 成为法人企业的标准词，较旧的义项则在固定说法中留存。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same bread-sharing root; group two holds other names for a firm.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「同吃面包」词根的词；第二组是企业的其他称呼。

entries.definition: A single person who accompanies another; company is the state or the group, not one companion.
entries.definitionCN: 指陪伴某人的单个个体；company 指状态或群体，不是单个同伴。

entries.definition: To go with someone or to play music alongside; the verb of the same root, not the business noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指陪同某人或为某人伴奏；同根动词，不是商业名词。

entries.definition: The relation of being companions; it names the bond, while company can name the people.
entries.definitionCN: 指同伴之间的关系；命名的是纽带，而 company 可以指人。

entries.definition: Simply more than one business; it counts firms, not companions.
entries.definitionCN: 只是不止一家企业；数的是公司，不是同伴。

entries.definition: A business, often a partnership of professionals; narrower and more formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业，常为专业人士合伙；范围更窄，语气更正式。

entries.definition: Trade in general or a trading organization; broader, and usable for the activity as well as the entity.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指买卖或商业组织；更宽，既可指活动也可指实体。

entries.definition: A company the law treats as one body, usually large; it adds legal structure that company lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 法律当作一个身体的公司，通常规模较大；加上 company 所缺的法律结构。

entries.definition: A business owned by two or more partners who share profits and liability; a form of company.
entries.definitionCN: 由两名以上合伙人共有、共享利润与责任的商业形式；是 company 的一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Those who share bread: a group becomes a companionship, then a firm.
normal.cn: 同吃面包的人：一群人先是同伴，后来成了企业。

normal.en: The family runs company, companies, companion, accompany and companionship.
normal.cn: 同族词有 company、companies、companion、accompany 与 companionship。

normal.en: Fixed phrases keep the old senses: keep somebody company, in good company, part company with.
normal.cn: 固定说法保留旧义：陪伴某人、与优秀的人为伍、与某人分开。

normal.en: A company of actors and a company of soldiers are both groups, not businesses.
normal.cn: 一队演员与一个连的士兵都是群体，不是企业。

normal.en: Chartered merchant companies turned a group name into a business name.
normal.cn: 经特许的商人团体把群体名称变成了企业名称。

abstract.en: Picture a table where everyone tears from the same loaf.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，所有人从同一块面包上掰着吃。

abstract.en: Picture six desks pushed together, each with its own lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象六张桌子拼在一起，每张都有自己的台灯。

abstract.en: Picture a stage curtain rising on a group that has rehearsed together for years.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布升起，台上是一群排练了多年的人。

examples.en: The company moved its office above the old market.
examples.cn: 这家公司把办公室搬到了老市场上方。

examples.en: He kept me company while I waited for the train.
examples.cn: 我等火车时他一直陪着我。

examples.en: We have company tonight, so there will be six at the table.
examples.cn: 今晚有客人来，桌上会坐六个人。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one group of people: the firm, the state of being together, the guests, the shared activity, the military unit, the association, the theatre troupe, and the chartered merchant society.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一群人：企业、有人作伴的状态、来客、共同从事活动的一群、军队连队、交往关系、剧团，以及特许商团。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: people around one table, all eating from the same loaf.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子周围的人，都从同一块面包上取食。

branches.en: BEING TOGETHER: the state of company and the continuing association are one relation seen as state and as act.
branches.cn: 在一起：作伴的状态与持续的交往，是同一关系作为状态与动作的两面。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE PRESENT: guests in a house and a troupe on a stage are groups gathered for an occasion.
branches.cn: 在场的人：家里的来客与台上的剧团，都是为某个场合聚起来的人。

branches.en: BODIES OF PEOPLE: soldiers under a captain and merchants under a charter are both organized groups.
branches.cn: 人的团体：上尉统领的士兵与特许状下的商人，都是有组织的群体。

branches.en: FIRM: the group that shares a livelihood becomes the everyday word for a business.
branches.cn: 企业：共享生计的一群人，成为企业的日常称呼。

branches.en: STAGE: performers keep the older group sense long after commerce took the word.
branches.cn: 舞台：商业占用这个词很久之后，表演者仍保留较旧的群体义。

intro.en: Company is a Latin bread word carried through French; the same root builds companion and accompany.
intro.cn: company 是经法语传来的拉丁「面包」词；同一词根构成 companion 与 accompany。

latinIntro.en: Latin panis 'bread' underlies companio, companion and accompany; the prefix com- adds 'together'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 panis「面包」是 companio、companion 与 accompany 的基础；前缀 com- 增添「共同」。

items.example: The root pictures a shared loaf.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘一块共享的面包。

items.example: The prefix binds the sharers together.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把分享者绑在一起。

items.example: The companion ate at the same table.
items.exampleCN: 这位同伴在同一张桌边吃饭。

items.example: The company repaired watches.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司修理钟表。

items.example: Her companion waited outside.
items.exampleCN: 她的同伴在外面等。

items.example: The nurse accompanied the patient.
items.exampleCN: 护士陪同病人。

items.example: The dog offered companionship.
items.exampleCN: 这只狗带来了陪伴。

items.example: Three companies share the market.
items.exampleCN: 三家公司在同一市场经营。

senses.title: A business, especially a professional one
senses.definition: a business organization, especially a partnership of lawyers, accountants or consultants
senses.definitionCN: 商业组织，尤指律师、会计师或顾问的合伙事务所
senses.example: The accounting firm on the corner has only two partners.
senses.exampleCN: 街角那家会计事务所只有两位合伙人。
senses.why: The business noun comes from the Italian word for a signature, because a firm was known by the name signed over its door.
senses.whyCN: 表示企业的名词出自意大利语「签名」一词，因为商行靠门上签下的名字被人识别。

senses.title: Solid and hard to move
senses.definition: solid in structure, so that it does not shake, sink or give way easily
senses.definitionCN: 结构坚实，不易晃动、下陷或塌落
senses.example: The table was firm enough to hold the heavy press.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子足够结实，能承住那台重压机。
senses.why: The adjective comes from a Latin word for strong and steadfast, and its first physical sense is simply 'holding its shape'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词出自拉丁语中表示「强壮、坚定」的词，其最初的具体义就是「保持形状」。

senses.title: Decided and not likely to change
senses.definition: fixed in purpose or opinion, so that pressure does not change it
senses.definitionCN: 在目的或意见上固定，压力也不使其改变
senses.example: She was firm about leaving before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 她坚决要在暴风雨前离开。
senses.why: A thing that holds its shape becomes a person who holds a decision, and the same adjective covers both.
senses.whyCN: 保持形状的东西，变成坚持决定的人，同一个形容词涵盖两者。

senses.title: Steady in price or condition
senses.definition: used of prices, markets or conditions that are steady rather than falling
senses.definitionCN: 用于价格、市场或状况，表示稳定而不下跌
senses.example: Demand kept the market firm through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 需求使市场在整个冬天保持坚挺。
senses.why: A market that does not sag is firm in the same physical sense as a beam that does not bend.
senses.whyCN: 不下沉的市场，与不弯的梁在同一个具体意义上都是「坚固」。

senses.title: To make something solid
senses.definition: to press or compact something so that it becomes solid and stable
senses.definitionCN: 压紧或压实某物，使其变得坚实稳定
senses.example: They firmed the soil around the new post.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把新柱子周围的土压实了。
senses.why: The verb is the adjective turned into an action: causing something to hold firm.
senses.whyCN: 动词是把形容词变成动作：使某物保持坚固。

senses.title: To settle a plan or arrangement
senses.definition: to make a plan, price or arrangement definite and no longer open to change
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、价格或安排确定，不再可变
senses.example: We firmed up the dates before booking the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在订礼堂之前把日期敲定了。
senses.why: Making an arrangement firm is the same as making a material firm: it stops shifting.
senses.whyCN: 把安排变「坚固」，与把材料变坚固是一样的：它不再移动。

senses.title: Strong and steady in grip
senses.definition: used of a grip, step or touch that is strong and controlled rather than shaky
senses.definitionCN: 用于握力、脚步或触碰，表示有力且受控，而非发抖
senses.example: He took her hand in a firm grip.
senses.exampleCN: 他有力地握住她的手。
senses.why: A hand that does not tremble is physically firm, so the word describes controlled strength.
senses.whyCN: 不发抖的手在身体上是「坚固」的，因此这个词描述受控的力量。

senses.title: Strict and unyielding in rule
senses.definition: used of rules, discipline or control that are applied strictly and without relaxation
senses.definitionCN: 用于规则、纪律或管理，表示严格执行、不作放松
senses.example: The school kept a firm hand on late arrivals.
senses.exampleCN: 学校对迟到严格管理。
senses.why: Steadiness in purpose, applied to authority, becomes strictness that does not soften.
senses.whyCN: 目的上的坚定，用在权威上，就成了不松动的严格。

intro.en: Firm has two separate histories that look like one word: the business noun comes from Italian firma 'signature', while the adjective comes from Latin firmus 'strong, steadfast'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: firm 有两个看似同一个词的不同来历：表示企业的名词出自意大利语 firma「签名」，形容词则出自拉丁 firmus「强壮、坚定」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Firmus meant 'strong, stable, steadfast', and it built firmare 'to make strong', the source of the adjective and verb.
items.cn: firmus 意为「强壮、稳固、坚定」，并构成 firmare「使坚固」，是形容词与动词的来源。

items.en: Italian firma meant 'signature', and a firm was originally the name signed at the head of a business, hence the trading house itself.
items.cn: 意大利语 firma 意为「签名」，firm 原指商号顶端签下的名字，后来指商号本身。

items.en: English borrowed the business noun in the eighteenth century, first for a commercial house and later for professional partnerships.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入这个商业名词，最初指商号，后来指专业合伙事务所。

items.en: The adjective arrived through Old French ferme, keeping the physical sense of solid and the moral sense of steadfast.
items.cn: 形容词经古法语 ferme 进入英语，保留了「坚实」的具体义与「坚定」的道德义。

items.en: The two histories converged in spelling, and only the context tells whether firm means a business or a quality.
items.cn: 两条来历在拼写上汇合，只有上下文能判断 firm 指企业还是一种性质。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like firm but belong to other families; group two holds other names for a business.
note.cn: 第一组是形近但属其他词族的词；第二组是企业的其他称呼。

entries.definition: The adverb from the adjective, meaning in a solid or decided way; it has no business sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由形容词构成的副词，意为牢固地或坚定地；没有商业义。

entries.definition: The quality of being solid or decided; a noun, unlike the business firm.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚固或坚定的性质；是名词，与表示企业的 firm 不同。

entries.definition: Built on the same Latin adjective, meaning to strengthen or make certain; it is not a business.
entries.definitionCN: 同出这个拉丁形容词，意为加强或确认；不指企业。

entries.definition: From Old English feorm, 'provisions or rent', not from the Latin adjective; the similarity is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 出自古英语 feorm「给养、地租」，并非出自那个拉丁形容词；相似只是巧合。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a business of any size; firm often suggests a professional partnership.
entries.definitionCN: 任何规模企业的日常说法；firm 常暗示专业合伙。

entries.definition: Trade itself or a trading organization; it is broader than firm and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 指买卖本身或商业组织；比 firm 更宽、更不正式。

entries.definition: A business owned jointly by partners; many firms are partnerships, but the words are not identical.
entries.definitionCN: 由合伙人共有的企业；许多 firm 是合伙，但两个词并不相同。

entries.definition: The office or business of a lawyer or doctor; close to firm in professional use.
entries.definitionCN: 指律师或医生的执业机构；在专业语境中接近 firm。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: The business noun is a signature, the adjective is a strong thing: two histories, one spelling.
normal.cn: 表示企业的名词是「签名」，形容词是「坚固之物」：两条来历，一个拼写。

normal.en: The family runs firm, firms, firmly, firmness, confirm and affirm.
normal.cn: 同族词有 firm、firms、firmly、firmness、confirm 与 affirm。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: a law firm, a firm decision, stand firm, firm up a plan.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各义项：律师事务所、坚定的决定、站稳立场、敲定计划。

normal.en: The adjective keeps a physical sense and a moral sense at once.
normal.cn: 这个形容词同时保留具体义与道德义。

normal.en: Farm looks similar but comes from an Old English word for provisions.
normal.cn: farm 形近，却出自古英语中表示给养的词。

abstract.en: Picture a stone pressed into soft ground, refusing to move.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头压进软土，怎么也不动。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a table that does not tremble while everyone else argues.
abstract.cn: 想象众人争论时，桌上有一只手始终不抖。

abstract.en: Picture a name signed once at the top of a page and trusted ever after.
abstract.cn: 想象页首签下一个名字，此后一直被人信赖。

examples.en: She joined a firm that advises small exporters.
examples.cn: 她加入了一家公司，专门为小出口商提供咨询。

examples.en: The ground was firm enough for the crane.
examples.cn: 地面足够坚实，可以支撑起重机。

examples.en: He remained firm in his refusal to sign.
examples.cn: 他坚决拒绝签字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 石头压进土里，桌子与账本都稳稳不动 → 稳固、商行

root: 两个同形词：名词 firm 出自意大利语 firma「签名」，指以签名为标识的商行；形容词与动词 firm 出自拉丁 firmus「强壮、坚定」与 firmare「使坚固」。两者只在拼写上汇合。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow two histories: the professional business, the solid object, the decided mind, the steady market, the act of compacting, the settling of a plan, the steady grip, and the strict rule.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿两条来历展开：专业商行、坚实之物、坚定的心意、稳固的行情、压实的动作、敲定计划、稳固的握力，以及严格的规矩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone pressed into ground, holding a table and a ledger steady.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块压进土里的石头，把桌子与账本都稳稳托住。

branches.en: SIGNED NAME: a house known by the name over its door becomes the business itself.
branches.cn: 签下的名字：靠门上名字被识别的商号，成为企业本身。

branches.en: SOLID: the object that holds its shape and the act of making it hold are one quality seen as state and action.
branches.cn: 坚实：保持形状的物体与使它保持的动作，是同一性质的状态与动作。

branches.en: STEADY PURPOSE: a decided mind and a controlled grip both refuse to tremble.
branches.cn: 坚定的目的：打定的主意与受控的握力，都不发抖。

branches.en: MARKET: a price that does not sag is firm in the physical sense.
branches.cn: 行情：不下沉的价格，在具体意义上就是「坚固」。

branches.en: FIXED IN PLACE: a settled plan and a strict rule both stop moving once fixed.
branches.cn: 固定下来：敲定的计划与严格的规矩，一旦定下就不再移动。

intro.en: The adjective firm is a Latin strong word; the business noun is an Italian signature word. Their families are different.
intro.cn: 形容词 firm 是拉丁语中表示「强壮」的词；表示企业的名词则是意大利语中表示「签名」的词。两个词族不同。

latinIntro.en: Latin firmus supplies firm, firmly, firmness, confirm and affirm; Italian firma supplies the business noun only.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 firmus 给出 firm、firmly、firmness、confirm 与 affirm；意大利 firma 只给出表示企业的名词。

items.example: The root pictures something that does not give way.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘不塌下的东西。

items.example: The verb names the act of making firm.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名「使坚固」的动作。

items.example: The name signed over the door identified the house.
items.exampleCN: 门上签下的名字标识了这家商号。

items.structure: firma > English noun; firmus > English adjective
items.example: The firm has two partners.

definition_zh: 组织；机构；企业；编排；整理；组织结构
definition_en: a group of people with a particular purpose and structure, or the act of arranging things into an ordered system
core_image: 一张桌上摊开的机构图，方框之间用直线连成层级，没有一处悬空
scene: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处。The international organization keeps offices in three countries.
sceneCN: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处；句中的 organization 指「为特定目的而设立的机构」（第 2 个义项：机构、团体）。图中可辨识物件：机构图、办事处门牌、文件夹、地球仪。

pos.zh: 组织；机构；企业；编排；整理；组织结构

senses.title: A group with a purpose and a structure
senses.definition: a group of people working together with defined roles towards a shared aim
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目标而按既定角色协作的一群人
senses.example: Every organization needs someone to keep the records.
senses.exampleCN: 每个组织都需要有人保管记录。
senses.why: The word comes from the Greek word for a tool, and an organization is a group arranged like an instrument for a purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自希腊语中表示「工具」的词，组织就是为某个目的像器具一样被安排起来的一群人。

senses.title: An institution or body
senses.definition: an established body such as a charity, a union, a hospital or an international agency
senses.definitionCN: 已设立的机构，如慈善团体、工会、医院或国际机构
senses.example: The international organization keeps offices in three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处。
senses.why: Once a group acquires a name, rules and premises, it is spoken of as an institution rather than a gathering.
senses.whyCN: 当一群人有了名称、规则与办公场所，人们就说它是机构，而不只是一次聚会。

senses.title: A company treated as a body
senses.definition: a business viewed as a structured body of departments, staff and procedures
senses.definitionCN: 被视为由部门、人员与流程构成的企业
senses.example: The organization employs four hundred people across six sites.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业在六个地点雇了四百人。
senses.why: Calling a firm an organization shifts attention from its trade to its internal arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 把企业称作 organization，注意力就从它的买卖转到它的内部安排。

senses.title: The act of arranging something
senses.definition: the act of putting parts, events or tasks into a workable order
senses.definitionCN: 把各部分、活动或任务排成可运作次序的动作
senses.example: The organization of the festival took six months.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆的组织工作花了六个月。
senses.why: Before the word meant a body, it meant the act of giving parts an order, and that act still carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 在指团体之前，这个词指「给各部分定次序」的动作，这个动作至今仍用这个名称。

senses.title: The structure itself
senses.definition: the pattern of departments, ranks and reporting lines inside a body
senses.definitionCN: 机构内部部门、层级与汇报线的格局
senses.example: The new director redrew the organization within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管在一年内重画了组织结构。
senses.why: If organizing is giving order, the resulting order is also called by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 如果组织是赋予次序，那么产生的次序也用同一个名称。

senses.title: The quality of being orderly
senses.definition: the quality of doing things in an ordered, planned way
senses.definitionCN: 以有序、有计划的方式做事的性质
senses.example: Her organization kept the whole project on schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 她的条理性让整个项目按计划推进。
senses.why: A person can possess the same order that a body has, so the noun also names a personal capacity.
senses.whyCN: 一个人也可以拥有团体那样的秩序，因此这个名词也指个人能力。

senses.title: The arrangement of living tissue
senses.definition: the structured arrangement of cells and tissues in a living body
senses.definitionCN: 活体中细胞与组织的结构安排
senses.example: The microscope revealed the organization of the leaf tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜显示出叶片组织的构造。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the word for the ordered arrangement of parts in a living thing, from the same tool image.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用这个词，指活体中各部分有序的安排，仍沿用「器具」的意象。

senses.title: An international body
senses.definition: a body set up by states or by agreement across borders to handle shared matters
senses.definitionCN: 由国家设立或跨国协议建立、处理共同事务的机构
senses.example: The organization was founded to coordinate relief after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国际组织是为协调战后救济而设立的。
senses.why: States needed permanent instruments for shared work, and the tool sense of the root fits that role exactly.
senses.whyCN: 各国需要为共同事务设立常设工具，词根的「器具」义正好契合这一角色。

intro.en: Organization comes from organize, built on Latin organum 'instrument', from Greek organon 'tool'. It first named the act of arranging and later the body so arranged. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: organization 来自 organize，其基础是拉丁 organum「器具」，再溯至希腊 organon「工具」。它先指安排的动作，后指被安排成的团体。年代均为约数。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument', and Greek philosophy used it for an instrument of reasoning as well as a physical tool.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，希腊哲学既用它指推理的工具，也指实物器具。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument, and it also named a musical instrument and, later, a bodily organ.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum 指器具，也用来指乐器，后来又指身体器官。

items.en: The verb organize meant to give parts an order so that they work together, like fitting tools to a task.
items.cn: 动词 organize 意为给各部分定次序使它们协同运作，像把工具配到一项任务上。

items.en: In English organization first named the act of arranging; by the eighteenth century it named the body that results.
items.cn: 在英语中，organization 先指安排的动作；到十八世纪才指由此形成的团体。

items.en: Industrial and international bodies made the word the standard term for any structured group, from charities to agencies.
items.cn: 工业与国际机构使这个词成为任何有结构团体的标准称呼，从慈善团体到政府机构。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same organ root; group two holds words for structured groups.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「器具」词根的各种形式；第二组是表示有结构团体的词。

entries.definition: To arrange things or people into order; the act behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物或人排成次序；是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: A part of a body or a musical instrument, from the same tool word; it is not a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体器官或乐器，同出「器具」一词；不是团体。

entries.definition: An individual living being, whose parts are organized; it is a creature, not an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个活体，其各部分有组织；是生物，不是机构。

entries.definition: Relating to an organization or its structure; it describes, while organization names.
entries.definitionCN: 与组织或其结构有关的形容词；描述性质，organization 命名实体。

entries.definition: An established body or custom with social standing; it stresses endurance, not internal arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指有社会地位的既定机构或惯例；强调持久，不强调内部安排。

entries.definition: A group of people joined for a shared interest, usually voluntarily; often smaller than an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 指为共同兴趣自愿结合的一群人；通常比 organization 小。

entries.definition: Any group treated as a unit, such as a governing body; it is vaguer about structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指被当作单位处理的任何群体，如管理机构；对结构说得更含糊。

entries.definition: A business, usually a professional partnership; it cannot name a charity or an agency.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业，通常是专业合伙；不能指慈善团体或政府机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Greek for tool: a group arranged like an instrument for a purpose.
normal.cn: 希腊语意为「工具」：为某个目的像器具一样被安排起来的一群人。

normal.en: The family runs organize, organization, organizational, organizer and organism.
normal.cn: 同族词有 organize、organization、organizational、organizer 与 organism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: a non-profit organization, an international organization, the organization of work.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各义项：非营利组织、国际组织、工作的安排。

normal.en: The same root gives organ, a body part that is itself a tool.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 organ，即本身就是「工具」的身体部件。

normal.en: The word first meant the act of arranging, then the body arranged.
normal.cn: 这个词先指安排的动作，后指被安排成的团体。

abstract.en: Picture a chart of boxes joined by straight lines, none of them floating.
abstract.cn: 想象一张方框图表，方框之间用直线相连，没有一个悬空。

abstract.en: Picture a toolbox where every tool hangs in its own marked place.
abstract.cn: 想象一只工具箱，每件工具都挂在标好的位置上。

abstract.en: Picture a choir that breathes together without anyone shouting.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，没人喊叫却一起换气。

examples.en: The organization trains volunteers to teach reading.
examples.cn: 这个组织培训志愿者教阅读。

examples.en: Poor organization wasted half the budget.
examples.cn: 糟糕的统筹浪费了一半预算。

examples.en: She is known for her organization and calm under pressure.
examples.cn: 她以有条理和临压不乱而出名。

root: 拉丁 organum「器具」，来自希腊 organon「工具」；动词 organize 指给各部分定次序，organization 由「安排的动作」引申为「被安排成的团体与结构」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one instrument: the purposeful group, the institution, the company as a body, the act of arranging, the structure, the personal orderliness, the living tissue, and the international body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一件「器具」：有目的的团体、机构、作为组织看待的企业、安排的动作、组织结构、个人的条理性、活体组织，以及国际机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an instrument whose parts fit together so that it can do one job.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件器具，各部件互相咬合，从而能完成一项工作。

branches.en: GROUP AS TOOL: a purpose-driven group and a company seen as a body are the same instrument at different legal sizes.
branches.cn: 作为工具的群体：为目的一组人与被视为身体的企业，是同一器具的不同法律规模。

branches.en: LASTING BODY: a charity and an international agency are institutions built to keep working.
branches.cn: 持久的身体：慈善团体与国际机构都是为持续运作而建的机构。

branches.en: FITTING TOGETHER: before there is a body there is the act of giving parts an order.
branches.cn: 装配：在团体存在之前，先有给各部分定次序的动作。

branches.en: THE ORDER ITSELF: the pattern of departments and reporting lines is the result of arranging.
branches.cn: 次序本身：部门与汇报线的格局，是安排的结果。

branches.en: NATURAL ORDER: a tidy person and living tissue both show parts kept in working order.
branches.cn: 自然秩序：有条理的人与活体组织，都显示各部分保持运作秩序。

intro.en: Organization is a Greek tool word plus a Latin action suffix, a common pattern in academic English.
intro.cn: organization 是希腊语「工具」词加拉丁动作后缀，是学术英语中常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon passed into Latin as organum, giving organ, organize, organization and organism.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 进入拉丁作 organum，给出 organ、organize、organization 与 organism。

items.example: The root pictures a tool fitted to a task.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘配到任务上的工具。

items.example: The word covered tools and organs alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个词同时涵盖器具与器官。

items.example: The heart is an organ.
items.exampleCN: 心脏是一个器官。

items.example: They organized the files by year.
items.exampleCN: 他们按年份整理了档案。

items.example: The organization keeps three offices.
items.exampleCN: 这个组织设有三个办事处。

items.example: The chart shows the organizational structure.
items.exampleCN: 这张图显示组织结构。

items.example: The organizer booked the hall.
items.exampleCN: 组织者订下了礼堂。

items.example: A cell is part of an organism.
items.exampleCN: 细胞是生物体的一部分。
